News.title: Musician, pregnant wife and daughter, 3, shot dead as chilling vid shows killer prowling before sick massacre
News.content:
THIS is the disturbing moment an alleged serial killer briefly showed his face to the CCTV inside a lift before assassinating a famous musician, his wife and their toddler.

Footage shows the suspect – hiding his identity behind a baseball cap and sunglasses – turning to the camera for a split second while on his way to the luxury penthouse where his unsuspecting victims awaited.



The bloodshed happened in an upscale neighbourhood near Mexico City, where Jonathan Meléndez, the keyboardist of the well-known indie rock band Camilo Séptimo, lived with his family.

As soon as the killer entered their home, he shot dead their nanny in the back.



Police believe he ordered Jonathan’s pregnant wife, Ana Paula Barragan, to muzzle the family dog so its barking did not alert the neighbours.

Ana and the couple’s youngest child Sofi, aged three, were then tied up and shot in the head using a gun with a silencer.

When the musician returned home, he witnessed the bloodied bodies of his wife and daughter, and fought the assassin – until he was overpowered and also gunned down.

Only the couple’s six-year-old boy survived the massacre, which happened on Tuesday afternoon.



Petrified but unharmed, the child was found hidden under a bed.

Two men have since been arrested in connection with the brutal killings.

One of them, identified as Diego Sebastián “N,” is accused of being the probable perpetrator, the prosecutor’s office said.

He is believed to be an associate of the musician and the pair apparently rowed over money.

Another man identified as Gerardo “N” is also under investigation for his alleged involvement.



Both allegedly took advantage of one of their “relationships of trust with the victims” to gain access to the gated residence.

Confirming the arrests and naming the suspects only partially, State of Mexico prosecutors said in a statement: “The two alleged perpetrators of the murders of four people and the killing of a dog in Atizapan de Zaragoza have been arrested.

“On Wednesday morning Diego Sebastian ’N’, identified as J.S.M.O.’s partner, and the probable perpetrator of the multiple homicide was arrested.



“Previously Gerardo ’N’ was arrested, also under investigation for his probable involvement in the same events.”

Jonathan’s group, referencing him by his nickname of Jonas, paid tribute to him and his loved ones after learning of their deaths.

“We will always remember Jonas with immense love and gratitude,” they said.

“Today we honour and celebrate his life, his music, his light, and all that we shared with those of us who were fortunate enough to know him and walk alongside him.

“We extend all our love to his family, friends, and loved ones during this time of immense sadness. We also extend our condolences to the family of Aleyda Romero, who worked with them.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jonathan was a founding member of Camilo Septimo in 2013.

News.title: Russian general in charge of Putin’s nuke bombers ‘shot in face & stomach’ in suspected Ukrainian assassination bid
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GUNNED DOWN Russian general in charge of Putin’s nuke bombers ‘shot in face & stomach’ in suspected Ukrainian assassination bid

A RUSSIAN general in charge of Vladimir Putin’s nuclear bomber fleet is fighting for his life after reportedly being shot in the face and stomach.

Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, 56, commander of Russia’s 22nd Heavy Bomber Aviation Division, is said to be in a “critical condition” after the suspected Ukrainian assassination bid.



Varpakhovich was gunned down with a pistol in the village of Probuzhdeniye, in Engels district, according to local reports.

A lone shooter is believed to have rushed the war chief as he left his home and fired two shots.



The suspect quickly fled the scene on a motorcycle as a helmet covered his identity.

A severely injured Varpakhovich was immediately rushed to hospital for life-saving surgery to remove the bullets, say Russian reports.



He was then reportedly escorted to Moscow on a medical evacuation flight. for further treatment.

Varpakhovich’s personal driver was also injured in the shooting but managed to escape, reports Mash.

No one has claimed responsibility for the brazen attack.

Varpakhovich has been accused of war crimes during the Ukraine war on several occasions.



Ukraine’s SBU security service claimed Varpakhovich ordered a deadly strike on Kyiv’s Okhmatdyt children’s hospital in July 2024.

Two people were killed and dozens wounded in the heinous attack on civilians.

He was also blamed for an April 2022 strike on an Odesa apartment block, which killed eight people.

News.title: Mum sobs as she appears in court with 4 others after tragic newborn daughter ‘knifed 15 times & left on washing machine’
News.content:
BABY 'MURDER' Mum sobs as she appears in court with 4 others after tragic newborn daughter ‘knifed 15 times & left on washing machine’

A MUM sobbed as she appeared in court along with four others after her tragic newborn daughter was allegedly stabbed 15 times and left on a washing machine.

Andrea Skopova, 20, was charged following the horrific discovery at a house in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, on Sunday.



She sobbed as she appeared at Sheffield Crown Court today along with four others – including a 15-year-old girl.

Skopova, Peter Horvath, 19, Peter Horvath, 38, and Nina Horvathova, 37, are all charged with murder, causing or allowing the death of a child and perverting the course of justice by taking steps to conceal the killing of an infant.



The teen girl, who cannot be named for legal reasons, is charged with perverting the course of justice.

All five defendants, who are Slovakian nationals, were watched from the public gallery by 26 members of their family.



Judge Sarah Wright fixed a trial date for April 12 next year, saying it was expected to last six to seven weeks.

Judge Wright remanded all the defendants in custody and fixed the next hearing for October 2.

The court was told yesterday that the tot – named as Baby S – suffered 33 injuries including from 15 “separate stabbings” to her “face and torso – front and back”.

She was then allegedly wrapped in a towel and in a blue bag and dumped on top of a washing machine in outhouse, it was said.



Prosecutor Luke Hopkinson said the baby’s mum is the defendant Andrea Skopova.



She is the girlfriend of the Horvath Jnr, who is the son of the other two adult defendants, but he is not believed to be the baby’s father.

Two women, aged 26 and 37, who were arrested on suspicion of murder remain on bail.

Officers remain in the area conducting enquiries as the murder probe continues.

Lauren Costello, Deputy Chief Crown Prosecutor at CPS Yorkshire and Humberside, said: “The Crown Prosecution Service has decided to prosecute four individuals with murder following a police investigation into the death of a newborn baby girl in the Wincobank area.

“A fifth person has also been charged with perverting the course of justice.



“Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and that it is in the public interest to pursue criminal proceedings.

“We have worked carefully with South Yorkshire Police as they carried out their investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendants are active and they have the right to a fair trial.

“It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information online which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings.”

News.title: Boy, 15, who stabbed female teacher in head with kitchen knife after following her into empty classroom locked up
News.content:
SCHOOL HORROR Boy, 15, who stabbed female teacher in head with kitchen knife after following her into empty classroom locked up

A TEEN boy who stabbed a female teacher in the head after following her into an empty classroom has been locked up.

The 15-year-old brought the kitchen knife to Milford Haven Comprehensive School in Pembrokeshire, Wales.



He then approached Vicki Williams’ desk and asked her to check some of his work.

The teen, who can’t be named, then pulled a large kitchen knife from his bag and stabbed the history teacher in the head.



A “violent struggle” ensued in which Vicki “screamed blue murder” and eventually succeeded in taking the knife from him.

The boy has now been sentenced to four-and-a-half years in youth detention after he was found guilty of wounding with intent but cleared of the more serious charge of attempted murder.



Sentencing, Judge Paul Thomas KC said: “I don’t know why you attacked Mrs Williams with that knife, you never told anybody why you did it.

“What I do know for certain is that you took a knife that day to school because you wanted to really hurt her with it.

“What I do know for certain is that you took a knife that day to school because you wanted to really hurt her with it.

“It was pure luck that she did not have far worse injuries, maybe even fatal injuries.



“You could have killed her, although the jury found that you didn’t mean to go that far.”

Swansea Crown Court heard the defendant launched “a sustained assault” at the 1045-pupil secondary school in February.

Vicki told the court how he was “cold” and “alarm bells” began to ring in her head when he shut the door to the classroom.

She also said in her evidence how she feared she was “dying” after the stabbing.

The jury was shown CCTV of the teen leaving the school premises following the horror.



He fled to his grandmother’s home, telling her: “Something went in my head, nan.”

Vicki was taken to hospital with a wound to her scalp, scratches on her back and minor cuts to her hands.

Christopher Rees KC, prosecuting, had argued the boy would have “continued this murderous attack” if Vicki did not wrestle the knife away.

He added: “He knows the truth about what he did, he just doesn’t have, I’m afraid, the courage or the remorse to tell anyone about it.

“He brought the knife into school because he planned to attack the teacher.



“Why Vicki Williams? Well, she was, at quarter past three, a lone female teacher, she was an easy target.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He’s not attacked a male teacher, has he? He’s attacked one of the young female teachers, alone in her classroom.”

The jury reached a majority verdict of 11 to one to convict the boy of wounding with intent after just over four hours of deliberation.

News.title: Bizarre moment two mice stand up & spar each other on Tube platform in front of creeped out commuters
News.content:
THIS is the moment two mice were caught squaring up to each other in a fight on a busy Tube platform.

The video shows the two critters engaging in a fist fight over a food item on the platform edge.



Standing on their back legs, the London mice contended against one another, circling around something on the floor.

After a few minutes, one of the rodents eventually retreats.



Determined to not give up, the second mouse circles back around.

However it eventually scurries away once again out of view of the camera.

As well as a source of entertainment for those waiting for their tube to arrive, the mice also became online sensations.

People were quick to comment on the match, noting their “petite” efforts.

One person said: “I hope they took care of their little ringside credentials.”

Another said: “I don’t know whether to laugh or cry.”



A third said: “My money is on the left mouse.”

A fourth joked: “At least they’re fighting behind the yellow line.”

This isn’t the first time mice fighting has caused a stir online.

In 2019 two squabbling critters were photographed and shortlisted for Wildlife Photography of the Year.

Sam Rowley captured the battle between the two city-dwellers before they scurried off with the crumbs and went their separate ways.

News.title: Man, 38, killed after being hit by 3 cars while walking on major motorway is pictured – as cops slam ‘incorrect rumours’
News.content:
CRASH HORROR Man, 38, killed after being hit by 3 cars while walking on major motorway is pictured – as cops slam ‘incorrect rumours’

A MAN who died after being hit by three cars while walking on the M56 has been pictured – as cops slam “incorrect rumours” about his death.

Krisstoffer Henshall, 38, was fatally struck on the motorway near Runcorn, Cheshire, in the early hours of Monday.



Police and ambulance crews descended on the eastbound carriageway at around 12.50am.

They discovered there had been a collision between Krisstoffer and three cars – a black Dacia Duster, a red Kia Niro and a black Ford Focus.



Despite the best efforts of paramedics, the 38-year-old was sadly declared dead at the scene.

Cheshire Police quickly launched a probe into his death and carried out enquiries at the scene, forcing the motorway to shut for several hours.

And the force has since launched a further appeal for information, while Det Sgt Russ Sime slammed “incorrect rumours” about the tragedy.

He said: “We are aware of a number of rumours circulating in relation to this collision, including reports that Kriss had been to Creamfields, which are simply incorrect.

“I would urge people not to speculate. This is an extremely difficult time for his family and friends, and our priority is to establish what took place.

“As part of the investigation we are appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident or believes they may have seen Kriss on the motorway prior to the collision, to get in touch.



“The same goes for anyone with any dashcam footage which may aid our investigation.

“Anyone with any information should contact Cheshire Police on 101 or via www.cheshire.police.uk/tell-us, quoting IML-2407733.”

Krisstoffer’s heartbroken family are being supported by specialist officers.

The M56 remained closed between Junction 12, for Runcorn, and Junction 14, for Chester services, before reopening at around 9.15am on Monday.

National Highways had confirmed a diversion route has been put in place while emergency services were dealing with the incident.



Issuing a statement on X, it said: “The M56 eastbound is closed between J14 (Hapsford) and J12 (Runcorn) for a police led incident.

“Cheshire Police lead the response to the ongoing incident and have closed the carriageway to allow emergency services to work at scene.

“National Highways have resources in attendance to assist with traffic management.

“Delays are likely on approach to the closure and diversion routes.”

News.title: People smuggling gangs ‘using mega-dinghies & doubling price for Channel crossings after running low on small boats’
News.content:
GANGS are turning to new tactics to illegally smuggle people into the UK after running low on small boats.

People smugglers are reportedly being forced to resort to “mega-dinghies” and have doubled the price for migrants to make the crossing.



It comes after mind-blowing pictures showed 230 migrants crammed onto a mega-dinghy arriving in the UK last month.

The average number of migrants per boat has increased tenfold since 2018 – as smuggling gangs continue to load more and more people on.



A BBC investigation has revealed this is because smugglers are running short of small boats.

Meanwhile, gangs are also hiking their prices to ferry migrants across the Channel, quoting around £1,700 per person – to be paid in cash.

The broadcaster reported one instance of how groups of migrants were collected along the coastline in northern France and jammed onto a single dingy.

After a total of five collections across three hours, it successfully made the crossing after 82 people, including children, had boarded the vessel.



Meanwhile, French police officers watched on as migrants who failed to make the trip trudged back to shore.

One woman said: “We regularly see people on the beach attempting the crossing.

“It feels like living in two parallel worlds that have nothing to do with each other; it’s really strange.”

The migrants will then have to wait for their next window of opportunity with charity workers telling the BBC many will sleep close to the beach instead of camps to boost their chances.

Two migrants, a Sudanese woman and an Afghan man, said they had attempted to make the crossing dozens of times.



Meanwhile, two Egyptian migrants who had been trying to cross for months explained how French authorities stopped them from doing so.

“The police stopped us from leaving and destroyed the boats,” one said.

One said he was trying to reach the UK so he could work and obtain his legal papers.

More than 16,513 people crossed the Channel between January 1 and September 1 this year, marking a 43 per cent decrease on the previous year.

Last month, shocking pictures laid bare the ever-increasing size of the so-called “small boats” – as vessels are now equipped to bring as many as 230.



The 49ft mega-dinghy that made the perilous journey in August carried more passengers than an average EasyJet flight.

It is a stark comparison to the vessels that arrived on British shores a decade ago, which were often canoe-sized row boats.

The average number of migrants per vessel has increased from seven to 67.6 over the past eight years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

More than £1billion has now been handed to France to help stopping Channel crossings.

An undercover reporter was able to cross the Channel in a small boat while posing as a migrant – and claims French police are giving smugglers free lifts back to the camps.

News.title: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem dies ‘peacefully’ at 92 ‘surrounded by loves ones’ as tributes paid to ‘one of a kind’
News.content:
FEMINIST icon Gloria Steinem has died at the age of 92.

The trailblazing journalist and activist, who became one of the most famous faces of the women’s liberation movement, died at her New York City home on Tuesday.



Her death was announced in a heartbreaking statement on Steinem’s official Instagram page on Wednesday.

“Yesterday, Gloria Steinem passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her,” it said.



“Gloria’s near-century on earth were years well-lived, and she continued working for equality until the very end.”

No cause of death was immediately revealed.

Steinem spent decades fighting for women’s rights and became one of the most influential figures of second-wave feminism from the 1960s onwards.

Her campaigning spanned reproductive rights, domestic violence prevention and gender inequality in the workplace.

Paying tribute to the legendary activist, her team said her ability to listen to others was her “greatest gift”.

“Her words, actions, and example gave people permission to be their truest selves,” the statement said.



“Gloria lived true to her independent spirit, always with curiosity and a great sense of humor.”

Steinem continued writing and campaigning into her later years and regularly welcomed people into her Manhattan home for “Talking Circles”.

Her team said the tradition would continue after her death.

She was also working on a forthcoming book, An Unexpected Life.



Steinem shot to national prominence in 1963 after going undercover as a Playboy Bunny to expose the working conditions endured by women at Hugh Hefner’s Playboy Clubs.

She spent weeks working at the New York Playboy Club before publishing her explosive account.



But it was her role in the burgeoning feminist movement that would make her an internationally recognised figure.

Steinem became a fierce advocate for expanding women’s rights at a time when huge inequalities remained entrenched in American life.

She helped push issues affecting women into the political mainstream as the movement fought against discrimination in education, employment, finance and reproductive healthcare.

Steinem was also a co-founder of Ms. magazine, which became a major voice of the feminist movement after its launch in the early 1970s.

Her decades of activism eventually earned her the Presidential Medal of Freedom, America’s highest civilian honour.



Then-President Barack Obama presented Steinem with the award in 2013.

Steinem also struck up an unlikely friendship with Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with the pair bonding over their shared interest in women’s rights.

The Duchess of Sussex previously revealed they became close after connecting during the Covid pandemic, and the pair later appeared together publicly to discuss female empowerment and political participation.

She and her older sister Susanne spent years travelling around the US with their parents as their father Leo worked as a travelling antiques salesman.

Steinem did not regularly attend school until she was 11, when her parents divorced and she returned to Ohio with her mother Ruth.



She later spoke about how watching her mother struggle with mental health problems – and seeing her concerns dismissed – helped shape her determination to give women a stronger voice.

Steinem went on to graduate from Smith College before embarking on the journalism career that would ultimately propel her onto the world stage.

Despite becoming synonymous with feminism, she continued campaigning for a broad range of equality and social justice causes throughout her life.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In announcing her death, Steinem’s team revealed that she had asked supporters wishing to honour her to donate to Gloria’s Foundation instead of sending flowers.

Her statement also recalled one of the activist’s favourite sayings: “The flap of a butterfly’s wing can change the weather hundreds of miles away.”

News.title: King Charles to welcome Sultan of Oman for State Visit as he returns to work after Balmoral break
News.content:
King Charles to welcome Sultan of Oman for State Visit as he returns to work after Balmoral break

The monarch will host Sultan Haitham bin Tarik at Windsor Castle in October as part of the leader’s three-day visit to the UK

View 3 Images King Charles is back to work after spending several weeks in Balmoral for the summer (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

King Charles and Queen Camilla will host the Sultan of Oman for a State Visit next month, as the monarch returns to his royal duties after spending several weeks in Balmoral for the summer break.

‌



The Royal Family’s social media accounts announced the upcoming State Visit, which will take place in October.

‌



Sharing a photo of the King alongside Sultan Haitham bin Tarik, the post read: “His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik, Sultan of Oman will pay a State Visit to the UK as the guest of Their Majesties The King and Queen from Tuesday 20th to Thursday 22nd October 2026,” alongside the flag emojis of the UK and Oman.

‌



Prince Harry and Meghan Markle rule out attending major Diana Award event after UK move READ MORE :

View 3 Images Charles with the Sultan of Oman in 2016 (Image: Getty Images)

While the official itinerary of the State Visit has yet to be announced, it is believed the Sultan’s visit will include a ceremonial welcome to Windsor, state banquet and the viewing of exhibits from the Royal Collection.

The Prince and Princess of Wales are likely to play a major part in the visit, as in the past few years, they have welcomed incoming world leaders upon their arrival on behalf of the monarch, and have sat alongside the King and Queen at state banquets.

‌



It is understood the invitation from the King was delivered to the Sultan in July, when the Oman leader met with then Prime Minister Keir Starmer at 10 Downing Street during an official visit to London.

The King met the Oxford-educated Sultan last July for tea at Windsor Castle during the foreign head of state’s private visit to the UK. During their meeting, the Sultan and King Charles reviewed the deep-rooted historical relations between their two nations.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Their discussions focused on how to enhance cooperation across various fields to serve mutual interests and future visions, while fulfilling the aspirations of both countries.

The last state visit by a Sultan of Oman to the UK was in March 1982 when Queen Elizabeth Il hosted Oman’s previous leader Sultan Qaboos bin Said.

Charles has made four official visits to Oman, the last in January 2020 when he travelled to Muscat to offer condolences after the death of Sultan Qaboos. The Prince and Princess of Wales have also visited the Middle Eastern country, as they made the trip in 2016 for a two-day visit.

‌



The last State Visit happened in March this year, when the King and Queen welcomed the President and First Lady of Nigeria to the UK. Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his wife, Oluremi Tinubu, undertook a three-day visit to Britain, where they were met by the Prince and Princess of Wales for an official welcome.

View 3 Images The last State Visit took place in March when the President of Nigeria and his wife were hosted by the King and Queen (Image: PA)

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

On the day of their arrival, Charles and Camilla invited their guests to view a special exhibition of items relating to Nigeria from the Royal Collection, in the Green Drawing Room of Windsor Castle. The group became particularly enthused by a tiny manuscript written by Sir Ben Okri, the Nigerian-born British poet, novelist and playwright who was the first black writer to win the Booker Prize.

The previous Nigerian state visit to the UK was in 1989, when Queen Elizabeth II welcomed military ruler General Ibrahim Babangida to London. For the March visit, the two-day event fell at the end of the holy month of Ramadan, during which many Muslims fast and refrain from eating or drinking between dawn and sunset – so there was no traditional lunch with the King in the castle for the president during the day.

News.title: UK travel company suddenly suspends all services as Brits 'stranded abroad'
News.content:
UK travel company suddenly suspends all services as Brits 'stranded abroad'

Wayfairer Travel has halted operations while taking steps to appoint an administrator, with holidaymakers due to travel this month warned not to go.

View Image Wayfairer Travel has halted operations with passengers due to travel this month warned not to go. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

A UK travel company has suspended all its services, with holidaymakers due to depart before the end of this month told not to travel.

‌



Wayfairer Travel, which specialises in holidays to destinations including the Maldives, Japan, Peru and Egypt, said its services had been halted “until further notice”.

‌



The company, founded in 2012, is seeking accounting and legal advice over its future as it moves to appoint an administrator. It said a formal update is expected this week.

‌



A spokesperson for Wayfairer Travel said: “We are truly sorry for the concern and uncertainty caused by the current situation.

“Wayfairer Travel has currently suspended all services until further notice.

“At this stage, we are unable to provide further information until we have received the appropriate accounting and legal advice.

‌



“These discussions are currently under way, and we expect to provide a formal update during the week commencing 31 August.

“We appreciate your patience and sincerely apologise that we cannot provide greater clarity at this time.”

The Association of Bonded Travel Organisers Trust (ABTOT) said it had been notified that Wayfairer was “unable to continue trading and is taking steps to appoint an administrator”.

‌



The organisation is now putting arrangements in place to assist eligible UK customers whose holidays have been affected.

ABTOT said: “Because Wayfairer cannot currently provide certainty that affected packages will be delivered, ABTOT is putting arrangements in place to assist eligible UK customers.”

Customers booked to depart on or before September 30, 2026, have been told “do not travel”.

Article continues below

Those whose holidays are scheduled after September 30 have instead been advised to wait for further information unless they are contacted with different instructions.

ABTOT added: “If your departure is after 30 September 2026, await further information unless you are contacted directly with different instructions.”

News.title: Nostalgic £6.50 cake on Tesco shelves is like stepping back in time to your childhood
News.content:
Nostalgic £6.50 cake on Tesco shelves is like stepping back in time to your childhood

Tesco shoppers have been urged to sprint to their nearest supermarket to buy a £6.50 cake that feels just like stepping back in time to your childhood days at school

View 2 Images Tesco shoppers are sprinting to buy the nostalgic cakes (stock photo) (Image: Peter Fleming via Getty Images)

There are certain things from growing up that stick with you long after the years have passed. A familiar smell, a song from the radio, or the taste of something you haven't eaten in decades can bring a rush of memories flooding back in an instant. It turns out that one supermarket has quietly tapped into exactly that feeling - and shoppers are absolutely here for it.

‌



Tesco has become the unlikely destination for anyone feeling a wave of nostalgia lately. Word has been spreading across social media about a product that has caught people's attention and stirred up memories of younger, simpler times. Whether you loved your school days or simply look back on them with rose-tinted glasses, this discovery has been stopping people in their tracks.

‌



The item causing all the fuss is a £6.50 treat called School Cake and Custard, produced by The Little Bakery World. The pack contains 10 individual sponge squares - five vanilla and five chocolate - each decorated with icing and sprinkles, accompanied by a pot of custard nestled in the centre. Anyone who spent their lunch breaks queuing up for a slab of sponge cake drenched in bright yellow custard will immediately recognise what this is paying tribute to.

‌



Instagram user Lauren was among those to flag the find, sharing a video of the cakes and making clear she was already planning a trip to pick some up. She described them as "pretty" but had one clear request before she'd be fully satisfied - as she said there simply isn't enough custard included

She wrote alongside her video: "I immediately NEED. With more custard."

View 2 Images Vanilla cake with white icing is a school dinner staple (Image: Martyn Wetherelt via Getty Images)

‌



The box itself sets the scene nicely, with the description reading: "Delicious vanilla and chocolate school cakes with a custard dip. Enjoy hot or cold!" - though it's fair to say the custard-to-cake ratio has become something of a talking point among those who've already got their hands on a pack.

The single pot of custard sitting in the middle of the platter has proven to be the product's one significant sticking point, with many shoppers agreeing that you'll likely need to supplement it with extra if you want the full nostalgic experience.

One commenter said: "Definitely more custard required!"

‌



Another added: "That is not enough custard."

A third wrote: "Custard to cake ratio is crazy."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Not everyone is convinced the flavour will live up to the memory, however. Some shoppers have found that no modern recreation quite matches what they recall from the school canteen, no matter how close it looks.

Someone stated: "It never tastes like it, though. I can't find anywhere that tastes as it did."

Beyond Instagram, the cakes have been garnering plenty of attention across food discovery groups on Facebook, too. New Food Spotter UK shared a photo of the pack to a flurry of heart-eyed emojis, and with the temperature dropping, the idea of warming up a few of these sponge squares and ladling over some hot custard on a dark evening has clearly struck a chord.

‌



One person said: "Oh my god, for the cold winter nights!"

Another shared: "I need this."

How to make your own custard

If you pick up the school cakes and want to add more custard, you can follow the BBC Good Food recipe to make your own custard - which takes just 25 minutes and makes eight servings.

‌



Ingredients

200ml double cream

700ml whole milk

4 large egg yolks

3 tbsp cornflour

100g caster sugar

1 tsp vanilla extract

Method

Article continues below

Add the cream and milk into a large pan and bring the mixture to just below boiling point. While this is heating, whisk the yolks, cornflour, sugar, and vanilla extract together in a bowl. Once the milk and cream mixture has been heated, gradually pour it into the sugar mixture, whisking constantly to blend the two together.

Once combined, add the mixture back into the pan. Heat it gently while stirring with a wooden spoon until the custard has thickened, but before any lumps form. Serve hot over your slices of cake and enjoy.

News.title: Spain urgent heat alert as areas packed with Brit tourists face up to 43C
News.content:
Spain urgent heat alert as areas packed with Brit tourists face up to 43C

Temperatures of 40C or higher are set to hit parts of mainland Spain - just days after Spanish weather service AEMET said it was 'virtually certain' that this summer was the hottest on record

View 4 Images Spain is battling a fresh heatwave (file image) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Temperatures of 40C or higher are set to hit parts of mainland Spain as the country swelters in a fresh heatwave.

‌



The heatwave began on Wednesday and is expected to last until Friday, with Spain's state weather service AEMET issuing orange weather alerts across large parts of the country, particularly in the south. The alerts, in place from 1pm until 8.59pm local time on both Thursday and Friday, warn that weather conditions pose an "important hazard".

‌



Spain's Civil Protection service issued a warning on Tuesday over "very high and persistent temperatures" expected to last until Friday. It said the risk of wildfires would rise again to "extreme levels", with possible dry afternoon storms adding to the danger. Wildfires have burned through more than 295,000 hectares in Spain so far this year.

‌



Thursday is expected to be the hottest day, with temperatures soaring to 43C in Seville, 42C in Córdoba and Jaén, and 40C in Cádiz, Granada and Huelva.

View 4 Images A map shows the orange weather warnings issued by AEMET for parts of Spain on Thursday (Image: AEMET)

On Friday, the extreme heat will spread into northern and eastern Spain, while easing in parts of the south - although temperatures are still forecast to reach 42C in Córdoba, 41C in Seville and 40C in Jaén.

‌



Parts of Ciudad Real, Cáceres and Badajoz are also expected to hit 40C, while Barcelona, Toledo, Huesca, Zaragoza, Ávila, Lleida, Tarragona, Navarra and La Rioja could see highs of 39C.

Meanwhile, parts of Madrid, Valencia, Castilla y León, Castilla-La Mancha and Extremadura are likely to see temperatures between 37C and 38C.

AEMET said the heat could continue for several more days beyond Friday, although temperatures are expected to gradually ease.

‌



According to the weather service, the arrival of a DANA - a Spanish acronym for an isolated high-altitude depression - over the south-west of the Iberian Peninsula will draw a mass of warm, dry air carrying suspended dust across much of mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands.

View 4 Images Firefighters seen battling a wildfire in Collserola Natural Park, on the edge of Barcelona, on August 25 (Image: Marc Asensio Clupes/JNA via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Combined with high levels of sunshine, this will drive temperatures to "very high levels for the time of year", the Public Protection service warned.

‌



So far this year, Spain has recorded 5,232 heat-related deaths - the highest figure since the Daily Mortality Monitoring (MoMo) system began keeping records in 2015.

In August alone, 2,147 deaths were attributed to high temperatures, according to provisional data available on Monday.

This year's figure has already surpassed the previous annual record, set in 2022, when 4,789 heat-related deaths were recorded.

‌



The average temperature in mainland Spain between June 1 and August 31 was 26C - 2.5C above the 1991-2020 average, Spanish public broadcaster RTVE reported on Monday, citing AEMET data.

View 4 Images A map shows orange weather warnings issued by AEMET for parts of Spain on Friday (Image: AEMET)

At the end of last month, AEMET said it was "virtually certain" that 2026 will have been the hottest summer on record in mainland Spain.

Article continues below

It comes after a Met Office report published in May found that there is an 86 per cent chance that at least one year between 2026 and 2030 will be hotter than 2024, currently the planet's warmest year on record.

It also found that there is a 91 per cent chance that global temperatures will temporarily exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in at least one of the next five years.

If global warming exceeds 1.5C - the target limit set by the Paris Agreement - the risk of severe climate impacts rises sharply. These include ecosystem damage, species extinction, more extreme weather, food and water insecurity, heat-related deaths and the loss of ancient ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica, which would cause sea levels to rise dramatically.

News.title: Boy racer smashes into garden just seconds after seriously injuring pensioner
News.content:
Boy racer smashes into garden just seconds after seriously injuring pensioner

Mohammed Khan crashed his Volkswagen Gold into elderly Peter Jeffree's stationary car - the pensioner suffered cracked ribs, a cracked sternum and three fractured vertebrae

Watford: Doorbell camera captures moment driver smashes into front garden

This is the shocking moment a boy racer smashed into a garden just seconds after seriously injuring a 74-year-old man.

‌



Mohammed Khan, then 17, smashed his Volkswagen Gold into Peter Jeffree's stationary car in Watford, Hertfordshire, on September 5, last year. Video shows the Golf travelling at speed before overtaking a red Mazda moments before reaching a junction.

‌



Just seconds later, a loud bang could be heard as Khan's vehicle collided with Mr Jeffree's yellow Reliant Scimitar GTE. A separate piece of doorbell footage then captures the moment his Golf smashed into another car in a front garden.

‌



Mr Jeffree suffered three fractured vertebrae, cracked ribs, and a cracked sternum, while his classic car that he had owned for more than 40 years was "completely destroyed."

View 3 Images Khan smashed his vehicle into a stationary car (Image: CPS / SWNS)

At least 22 people killed and dozens injured in Egyptian holiday hotspot bus crash READ MORE :

Tiger Woods avoids jail with last-minute plea deal over reckless driving charge that ended in horror crash READ MORE :

"If I had anyone in my car, if my wife had been in the passenger seat and they had hit me in the middle of the car, we both could have been killed," he said. A court heard Khan, who had three friends in his car, was speeding at about 60mph on a 30mph residential road.

‌



He overtook another car at speed before he "shot across the junction without any hesitation" and crashed into Mr Jeffree's car. Khan, who is now 18, was sentenced at St Albans Crown Court on Friday last week after he pleaded guilty to causing serious injury by dangerous driving.

View 3 Images The teenage driver left a pensioner with serious injuries (Image: CPS / SWNS)

A sentence of 19 months at a Young Offenders' Institution (YOI) was suspended for three years. He was ordered to complete 250 hours of unpaid work and 15 days of rehabilitation activities.

‌



Khan was also given a three-year driving ban and must pass an extended retest before he can drive again. Prosecutor Nadine Mathurasangh told an earlier court hearing: “At around 2pm in the afternoon the defendant was driving a red Volkswagen vehicle on Stratford Way.

“He was seen to be driving at excessive speed. This was a 30mph zone and we’ve got a witness who says the approximate speed driven by the defendant was 60 to 70mph.”

View 3 Images Khan was sentenced to 19 months in a young offenders' institution (Image: CPS / SWNS)

Article continues below

As Khan approached the junction with Cassiobury Drive he performed a dangerous overtake of a red Mazda on the offside, the court heard. The lady driving the Mazda said Khan’s vehicle then “shot across the junction without any hesitation” and smashed into Mr Jeffree’s car.

Both vehicles were sent spinning – Khan's car ended up on somebody's front garden while Mr Jeffree’s came to a rest in the road. Defending, Amita Patel said her client was remorseful and had written a "heartfelt" letter of apology to Mr Jeffree.

In the letter, Khan wrote: "Since the accident I have thought about it a lot. I genuinely wish I could change what happened."

News.title: Boy who stabbed teacher in the head after asking her to check his homework is locked up
News.content:
Boy who stabbed teacher in the head after asking her to check his homework is locked up

The pupil attacked history teacher Vicki Williams at Milford Haven Comprehensive School in February

View 2 Images Teacher Vicki Williams was stabbed by a pupil at Milford Haven School in Pembrokeshire (Image: Milford Haven School)

A 16-year-old schoolboy who stabbed a teacher in the head at his school in Pembrokeshire after asking her to check his homework has been sentenced to four and a half years' youth detention.

Swansea Crown Court previously heard how the boy shut the teacher inside her classroom before launching a knife attack on her.

The boy, who cannot be named for legal reasons, had previously pleaded not guilty to attempting to murder Vicki Williams at Milford Haven Comprehensive School in February.

Today a judge at Swansea Crown Court sentenced him to four and a half years’ youth detention. He was previously found not guilty of attempted murder but guilty of wounding with intent. The boy had previously pleaded guilty to possessing a kitchen knife on the school grounds.

The pupil, who was 15 years old at the time, entered Ms Williams’ classroom at around 3pm on February 5. The court heard the pupil approached her desk and asked her to check some of his work.

It was when he shut the door to the otherwise empty classroom, saying it was cold, that "alarm bells" began to ring in her head. The jury was told the student then pulled a large kitchen knife from his bag, striking her in the head.

View 2 Images Police were called to Milford Haven Comprehensive School (Image: Google Maps)

The court heard a "violent struggle" ensued in which Ms Williams "screamed blue murder" and eventually succeeded in taking the knife from him.

Christopher Rees KC, prosecuting, told the hearing the boy launched a "sustained attack" on Ms Williams and would have continued had the teacher not disarmed him. Mr Rees told the jury: "(He) deliberately stabbed Vicki Williams to the head and continued the attack."

The boy ran out of the school but was later arrested at the home of a family member, the jury was told. Ms Williams attended Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest and was found to have sustained a wound to her scalp, scratches on her back and minor cuts to her hands. Mr Rees said: "The prosecution case is that the whole incident was planned by (the pupil).

"(He) closed the door because he wanted to isolate Vicki Williams so that he could attack her." Ms Williams later told police in an interview he said nothing when he "lunged at her". Mr Rees said: "(She said) she had never seen eyes like it. She described the look on his face as pure hatred."

The defendant, who was 15 at the time, was found guilty of wounding with intent after being acquitted by a jury of attempted murder. Passing sentence today, Judge Paul Thomas KC said it was “pure luck” Mrs Williams had not been seriously injured or worse.

“I don’t know why you attacked Mrs Williams with that knife, you never told anybody why you did it,” the judge said. “I think it may have been that in some way she had upset you, but I don’t know for certain why.

“What I do know for certain is that you took a knife that day to school because you wanted to really hurt her with it. “You knew what you were going to do was very wrong, but you had planned it in advance.

“You knew she would not be any physical match for you and when you stabbed her in the top of her head with the knife, you knew that at the very least that might cause her a great deal of harm.

Article continues below

“It was pure luck that she did not have far worse injuries, maybe even fatal injuries. You could have killed her, although the jury found that you didn’t mean to go that far.”

News.title: British couple killed in Lisbon funicular disaster remembered in heartbreaking tributes
News.content:
British couple killed in Lisbon funicular disaster remembered in heartbreaking tributes

The devasted families of couple Will Nelson and Kayleigh Smith have revealed the painful void left behind as they mark one year since the Lisbon disaster

View 3 Images Will Nelson and Kayleigh Smith were among 16 people killed in the Lisbon funicular disaster (Image: Cumbria Police / SWNS)

The families of a British couple killed in the Lisbon funicular disaster have told of the devastating hole left in their lives one year on from the tragedy.

‌



Will Nelson, 44, and Kayleigh Smith, 36, had been looking forward to an exciting future together when they boarded the Glória funicular in the Portuguese capital on September 3 last year. But the historic hillside tram derailed and ploughed into a building, killing the couple from Macclesfield and 14 others.

‌



Twelve months on, Will’s brother Gareth said losing his big brother and “idol” had made it the most difficult year of his life. He said: “This has been the most difficult year of my life. A living hell is the best description. It is still difficult to put into words how much Will is missed.

‌



View 3 Images Lisbon's Gloria Funicular was one of the Portuguese capital's most famous attractions (Image: Getty Images)

Canary Islands: More than 80 dead including baby after boat adrift for weeks at sea READ MORE :

“What I have learnt ever since this began a year ago is how much he meant not just to our family but to everyone who knew him. I know of so many occasions when friends and acquaintances have said when Will helped them, fought in their corner and unselfishly gave his time to help anyway he could. He and Kayleigh loved their theatre work and to hear that their legacy will be honoured in multiple ways in multiple places fills we with pride that you wouldn’t believe."

He added: "He was my big brother and idol, and I hope I can carry on his life mission to look after others.”

‌



Kayleigh’s family have also spoken of the “huge void” left by the couple as they joined a memorial event in Lisbon to mark the anniversary today. The 36-year-old had been at a hugely exciting point in her life before the trip. Just two weeks before the disaster, she had passed her master’s degree with distinction at Manchester’s Arden School of Theatre and was preparing for a career as a professional theatre director.

Her loved ones said she had battled undiagnosed ADHD for much of her life before finally receiving a diagnosis in 2022, but had gone on to achieve an enormous amount.

They said: “The last 12 months have been incredibly difficult for a lot of people connected with Kayleigh. Kayleigh and Will have left a huge void in our lives that cannot be filled and we will forever be reminded of that.

‌



“We are all so proud of her which makes it harder. She had just passed her master’s degree, with distinction, at the Arden School of Theatre in Manchester two weeks before the crash and was destined for a successful career as a professional theatre director having already won many awards and nominations during her theatre life.

View 3 Images A third British victim, Andrew David Kenneth Young, 82 also died in the disaster (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“She battled with undiagnosed ADHD all through her life until her eventual diagnosis in 2022 yet remained defiant and still achieved so much. She was a shining light and inspiration for the many people she helped and encouraged. At this point, she was the happiest she had ever been, and when she travelled with Will to Lisbon, they had many exciting plans for when they returned.

‌



“The love and support for us all has been overwhelming and we wish to thank our families, friends, professional bodies, and everybody in Kayleigh’s world. Our thoughts go out to all the families who have suffered as a result of this tragedy, the people of Kayleigh’s hometown of Macclesfield, and to the people of Lisbon. All the World’s A Stage – Shakespeare.”

The pair were among passengers travelling on the 140-year-old Elevador da Glória when disaster struck.

Investigators have since said an underground cable which snapped had only been acquired the year before the crash and had never been certified for passenger transportation. The cable acted as a counterweight between two carriages, according to Portugal’s Air and Rail Accident Investigations Bureau.

Article continues below

A third British victim, Andrew David Kenneth Young, 82, from Holyhead, Anglesey, also died in the disaster. He was a transport enthusiast.

Rebecca Gilmore, senior associate at law firm Hugh James, is supporting the families of all three British victims.

News.title: Man greets crowd at Trafalgar Square but stuns people when they notice who he is
News.content:
Man greets crowd at Trafalgar Square but stuns people when they notice who he is

A man was spotted greeting people at Trafalgar Square in London, but onlookers were left floored when they realised who it was. It's not every day you see such a star on the city's streets

View Image He greeted people at Trafalgar Square (stock image) (Image: Grant Faint via Getty Images)

A man recently left people floored after greeting crowds at Trafalgar Square, as many were left taken aback when they realised who he was. It may be normal to occasionally spot a famous face on the streets of London, but it's not every day you see such a star walking down the street.

‌



A video of the jaw-dropping encounter was shared by social media account Drone of London, and it swiftly went viral as followers couldn't quite believe who had rocked up at one of London's most iconic landmarks. Indeed, it seems many were taken by surprise as the star totally transformed their days by appearing.

‌



It wasn't long before he started to interact with fans, and spend some time with locals. It's not the first time a huge celebrity has been spotted in London either.

‌



The clip was shared with the caption: "NAHHHH. JAY-Z REALLY PULLED UP TO HIS TRAFALGAR SQUARE POP UP!"

In the footage, American rap icon Jay-Z can be seen making his way down the street and greeting fans warmly. He appeared to be thoroughly enjoying the sunshine and the buzz of the city.

Unsurprisingly, the video set tongues wagging online, with scores of people eager to have their say. Fans flooded the comments section with their reactions to the unforgettable moment.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

One wrote: "Great guy. I served him and Beyonce 20 years ago when I worked at Vuitton on Bond Street. He was really nice and funny. Can't wait for the show this Friday."

Another added: "Imagine getting this close. Wow."

‌



A third replied: "The GOAT." Meanwhile, a fourth commented: "Damn."

One more also noted: "Yeah, I will follow HOV until the wheels come off. I love me some Jay."

Why is he in London?

This week, rap icon Jay-Z is reported to have left fans stunned after turning up at an immersive installation in London's Trafalgar Square. It was launched to promote his forthcoming concerts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Article continues below

Jay, 56, is due to perform on September 4 and 5 as part of his Jay-Z 30 tour. The gigs will mark the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt, alongside the 25th anniversary of his sixth album, The Blueprint.

The installation features period televisions showing music videos, live performances and contemporary programming. The aim is said to be transporting audiences back to 2001, while capturing the cultural significance of The Blueprint era.

It's understood merchandise will also be available for fans to purchase. It's evident many weren't expecting to spot him this week though.

News.title: Watch: BBC witnesses 'taxi boat' picking up migrants multiple times in a day
News.content:
A BBC investigation has found smuggling gangs are running low on small boats, forcing rival gangs to have to work together to meet demand for crossings.

With crossings at a six-year low, it includes loading more migrants on larger vessels, as the 'mega-dinghies' that were first seen last month.

The gangs claim more are being prepared.

News.title: Zack Polanski says he'll run for former PM Starmer's seat in by-election
News.content:
Green Party leader Zack Polanski has confirmed he wants to stand in the by-election brought about by Sir Keir Starmer's resignation as an MP.

Polanski, who is currently a London Assembly member but not a member of Parliament, said he was "so excited by the prospect" of being the first Green MP for Holborn and St Pancras.

The Greens are targeting the seat, until now a Labour stronghold, after coming second to Labour in the area in local elections earlier this year.

Sir Keir announced on Tuesday that he was quitting as MP for the London constituency, two months after he stood down as prime minister, setting up a challenging by-election for his successor Andy Burnham.

In comments to the Camden New Journal, external on Thursday morning, Polanski said: "I have lived and worked in this community over many years, I know it well and I love it.

"It represents so many of the things that make London so special. I am so excited by the prospect of representing this place in Parliament."

He added: "It's a clear fight between Labour and the Green Party."

The Green Party currently has five MPs.

In order to officially be the Green candidate for the seat, Polanski needs to be selected by local party members - something his comments suggest will happen.

But there have been reports in recent days of splits among local Green activists, some of whom are said to favour a Palestinian candidate or a pro-Gaza independent.

And it is currently unclear whether Andrew Feinstein, the independent runner-up to Sir Keir in the constituency at the 2024 general election, will stand too which could split the vote.

A date has not yet been set for the by-election.

Sir Keir had been MP for the area since 2015, but said he was quitting to focus on a role in international affairs.

The former prime minister had previously said he would stay on as an MP until the next UK general election, which is not due until 2029.

He said it was the "right time" for him to "pass the baton to a successor".

"I will now focus on other things and that will be international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology in a fast-changing world," he said, adding he would also continue his work combatting violence against women and girls.

Sir Keir became prime minister after winning a landslide majority at the 2024 election, but quit No 10 after pressure from Labour MPs to stand aside.

Labour has not decided its candidate to potentially take on Polanski, with applications closing on Friday.

News.title: Watch: Uber launches UK's first robotaxis with a driver - here's what it's like to ride in one
News.content:
Customers in London can now travel in the UK's first robotaxis as Uber launches its self-driving minicab on Thursday - the company is the first to launch the service.

Initially, it only has 15 autonomous vehicles with a licence to operate in the city, and each one must have a human safety driver behind the wheel ready to take control if anything goes wrong.

At the moment, the UK fare for a robotaxi ride will be the same fare as a standard UberX, Uber Electric, or Uber Comfort journey, with upfront fares shown in the app.

The BBC's Zoe Kleinman was the first British journalist to hail a self-driving Uber in London - here's how the ride went.

News.title: Hundreds of North Sea workers too heavy for new helicopter rules
News.content:
Hundreds of North Sea workers are still too heavy for offshore helicopter travel less than two months before new rules come into force, BBC Scotland has learned.

From November they should weigh no more than 19st 7Ib (124.7kg) in their clothing and footwear, so they can be winched to safety in an emergency.

When the plans were announced by industry body Offshore Energies UK (OEUK) last year, they said more than 2,200 workers were above that limit. New figures suggest up to 800 still exceed it.

Jobs could be lost as a result, and an occupational health expert said some had left the offshore industry rather than lose the weight.

However an employment law specialist said alternative onshore roles could also be explored by companies.

News.title: Could Lindsay Clancy trial end in a mistrial? Here are the jury's options
News.content:
After a gruelling five-week murder trial, Lindsay Clancy's fate rests with 12 anonymous jurors. And they cannot make up their minds.

The jury of nine women and three men have told the judge, two days in a row, that they cannot reach a unanimous decision. Despite the judge's continued urging that jurors keep at it, the struggle has raised the prospect of a mistrial in Clancy's case.

"It is desired that the case be decided," Judge William Sullivan told the panel on Wednesday afternoon, after members sent him a second note saying they are undecided after five days.

He read a mandatory, formal set of instructions and sent them back - some with frustrated expressions on their faces.

The 36-year-old former nurse does not dispute that she killed her two sons and daughter in 2023 in the basement of their family home in Massachusetts. But her lawyer argues she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time, and therefore could not distinguish right from wrong.

The prosecution claimed Clancy made a calculated, intentional decision to kill them and knew right from wrong in that moment. She is charged with three counts of first-degree murder.

Under US law, the jury must unanimously reach a conclusion "beyond a reasonable doubt". If they cannot, the judge can call a mistrial, which ends the trial with no verdict.

This jury has several outcomes to choose from. Potential verdicts include not guilty, not guilty by reason of insanity, first-degree murder, second-degree murder, and manslaughter.

News.title: DVLA withdraws tax conviction against Sadiq Khan after he says it was a scam
News.content:
At a hearing before magistrates at Hereford Justice Centre on Thursday, the case was formally reopened against the mayor and withdrawn by the panel after a request from the DVLA.

Neither the mayor nor a representative from the DVLA were present at the court for the one-minute hearing.

The legal advisor told the panel of magistrates they may be aware of the case as it was "widely publicised" on Wednesday, adding: "The DVLA have requested that the original matter, if you consider it to be reopened, be marked withdrawn."

Chairwoman of the bench Mrs Digings JP said: "We accept the reopening of the case as requested.

"Further to the request from the DVLA, we are going to mark the matter as withdrawn."

Last month, a magistrate sitting in a private hearing of the Single Justice Procedure in Herefordshire convicted Khan in his absence and ordered that he pay a Â£220 fine, Â£85 in costs and settle the Â£35.84 bill for unpaid tax on the Micra.

Court documents showed letters regarding the unpaid road tax bill had been sent to Gordon Ramsay's east London restaurant instead of the mayor.

The DVLA said a letter asking for confirmation of the identity of the car owner, which was sent to the wrong address, went unanswered in January.

This led to a criminal prosecution on 18 August after no plea was entered to the charge.

The mayor's adviser said the DVLA would investigate the false registration of the car.
