News.title: Chris Mason: Reform face headwinds as they gather for conference
News.content:
Reform UK begin their annual conference in Birmingham a bigger party than they were a year ago, their numbers swelled at Westminster, at Holyrood, in the Senedd and in local authorities.

But they also gather amid significant political headwinds, much of which revolve around money.

There was that whopping Â£5m gift to Nigel Farage from Christopher Harborne, the Thailand based British billionaire, and the long running row about whether the money should have been declared by Farage once he became an MP.

Then there is, among other things, the Metropolitan Police investigation into donations to the party during the last general election campaign.

Reform insists that it "takes pride in its stringent vetting of donations."

When the party got together in the same West Midlands venue a year ago, they were an insurgency provoking intrigue and attention and demonstrating plenty of momentum.

Indeed that momentum was so significant that it was a major factor, perhaps the major factor, in accelerating the demise of Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister, because the potential prospect of a Reform government frightened the Labour Party to its core.

Would Starmer, its then desperately unpopular leader, help or hinder their attempts to take on Farage? Hinder was the eventually overwhelming view within Labour, and so Starmer was a goner.

But politics can change, and change quickly. With Starmer out and Burnham in, there is early evidence of some support for Labour picking up. No longer are Reform comfortably leading in all the opinion polls - in some they're not leading at all. Add to this a more confident and prominent Kemi Badenoch leading the Conservatives and the recent rise too of Restore Britain, the outfit set up by the former Reform MP Rupert Lowe. And the Scottish National Party and Plaid Cymru won and so beat them in the devolved elections in Scotland and Wales respectively. In other words, collectively Reform's opponents appear more energised and popular.

Make no mistake, no party at a UK wide level is popular at the moment, but the scrap appears more evenly matched than it did.

News.title: B&Q and Five Guys among firms that paid staff below minimum wage
News.content:
DIY store B&Q and the fast food chain Five Guys are among hundreds of UK businesses named by the government for paying staff below the minimum wage.

More than 600 employers were ordered to pay affected workers the outstanding wages, with Â£4m returned to workers, according to the Department for Business and Trade.

The firms have also been issued penalties worth Â£7m.

B&Q said the underpayments were unintentional and the result of calculations involving geographical allowances, while Five Guys blamed "technical differences in how payroll regulations were applied".

The list of 658 businesses includes shops, restaurants, nurseries, social care providers and a handful of NHS trusts. The government did not say over what time period the underpayments spanned.

Minimum wage is Â£12.71 for staff aged 21 and over. For 18 to 20 year olds the rate is Â£10.85, and for under 18s and apprentices it is Â£8.

B&Q underpaid 4,530 workers a total of more than Â£456,000, according to the government.

B&Q said in response: "The shortfalls in payments were unintentional. They relate to calculations involving geographical allowances which are paid in addition to minimum hourly rates. All affected colleagues were quickly paid in full in July 2025."

Five Guys, named in the list as owing over Â£54,000 to 3,699 staff, said "technical differences in how payroll regulations were applied" led to its underpayments, which were identified in a review by the HMRC, the UK's revenue and tax authority.

"We worked closely and transparently with HMRC throughout the process and have made all required payments to affected current and former employees," the company said.

Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group failed to pay over Â£123,000 to 75 workers, according to the list. BBC News understands the underpayments were the result of salary sacrifice schemes which have since been changed.

The government list said St George's University Hospitals in Wandsworth, London, underpaid 55 workers. It is understood that this was due to salary sacrifice schemes and technical issues with London weighting allowances for some staff. The group has since changed its processes following a review by HMRC.

BBC News understands that the Trust which covers the two groups disputes that any staff were underpaid.

A spokesperson said apprentices at Norfolk Community Health and Care NHS Trust were inadvertently underpaid between 2019 and 2023.

They said while their pay met the requirements for their contracted hours, meetings, handovers and time spent changing into uniform hadn't been accounted for, adding the trust has since changed policies and practices.

The other trust named has been contacted for comment.

There were also several nursing homes on the list, and multiple childcare providers.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the government was determined to stamp out the practice of "short-changing your staff".

"The best businesses know that looking after your workers isn't just the right thing to do, it's the smart thing to do," he said.

Kate Dearden, minister for the future of work, said: "Underpaying your staff is illegal, and we will not let workers foot the bill for their boss failing to follow the rules."

"Every employer should check their payroll now and reach out to Acas if they need further support," she added.

The first 10 employers on the government's list, which was sorted by the amount of wages not paid, are:

1. B&Q Ltd, failed to pay Â£456,934.72 to 4,530 workers.

2. Elysium Healthcare Holdings 3 Ltd, Borehamwood, failed to pay Â£330,048.81 to 1,095 workers.

3. St George's, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group, failed to pay Â£123,331.97 to 75 workers.

4. Support Staff Services Limited, Slough, failed to pay Â£119,715.13 to 323 workers.

5. Forest Holidays Ltd, Moira, failed to pay Â£100,308.68 to 598 workers.

6. St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London (Wandsworth), failed to pay Â£77,498.91 to 55 workers.

7. Lanes Group Limited, Leeds, failed to pay Â£67,893.34 to 297 workers.

8. UK Care Team Ltd, Leicester, LE19, failed to pay Â£67,082.76 to 99 workers.

9. Five Guys JV Limited, London (Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea), failed to pay Â£54,642.47 to 3,699 workers.

10. Merlin Cinemas Limited, Redruth, failed to pay Â£50,198.75 to 181 workers.

The list marks the first "naming round" since the Fair Work Agency was set up in April under the Employment Rights Act.

As well as enforcing the minimum wage, the agency also will soon tackle practices of denying workers holiday and sick pay.

Chair of the agency's advisory board, Matthew Taylor, said naming employers which underpay staff was an important reminder that "paying the minimum wage is not optional - it is the law".

He said: "Most employers want to do the right thing, and we will support them to comply, but those who fall short should expect robust enforcement to protect workers and maintain a fair playing field for responsible businesses."

Clarification 3 September: An earlier version of this article contained a direct quote from a spokesman for St George's, Epsom and St Helier Hospital Group which was later withdrawn. This section was amended to summarise the BBC's understanding of how salary sacrifice schemes had operated at the hospitals. It also incorporated the trusts' view that no staff had been underpaid.

News.title: Almost half of households do not see benefits of economic growth, report says
News.content:
Almost half of people in Britain live in areas where economic growth does not translate into a better quality of life with a "stark" North-South divide in the spending power of households, a new report finds.

Researchers at consultancy PwC said every region in the north of England, Midlands and Wales had lower spending power than the country's average, with London and the South East comfortably above.

The findings come as Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to tackle regional inequalities in a bid to boost living standards across the country.

But questions remain over the PM's plans, with surging government borrowing costs set to limit his room for manoeuvre at October's Budget.

The PwC report said the equivalent of 12.5 million households - 46% - lived in parts of the country where economic growth, often seen through increased business investment and job opportunities, was not leading to better living standards.

It said households in the north east of England had 6.6% less spending power than the national average, equivalent to Â£1,542 less a year. The North West was Â£1,493 less, while Yorkshire and the Humber were worst off with spending power down Â£1,917 comparatively.

Meanwhile, households in the South East were found to have spending power 9% above the national average, worth an additional Â£2,154 a year, followed by London.

Household spending power is seen as a good measure of whether economic growth is improving living standards.

PwC says it measures this by looking at income after taxes and housing costs, and takes into account the size and makeup of a household - which is aimed at giving a better idea of the money available to meet other expenses.

The UK has seen years of slow growth, although the economy expanded by 1.2% in the first six months of this year, according to official figures.

Economic growth usually means people spend more, extra jobs are created, more tax is paid to the government and workers get paid better.

In theory, this leaves people better off. But it takes time for the benefits to be felt, and it does not necessarily benefit everyone. According to PwC, "only a fraction" of a rise in GDP - the size of the economy - leads to increased spending power.

Researchers said while there was a clear North-South divide in the spending power of households, there were also examples of spending power differences within areas deemed better off, such as London and the south east.

For example, Richmond's average annual disposable income was the highest in London at Â£35,448 - almost double the Â£18,384 recorded in neighbouring Hammersmith and Fulham.

"The research shows just how differently prosperity is experienced across the UK, with stark variations not only between regions but on each other's doorstep," said Rachel Taylor, government and health industries leader at PwC.

News.title: Burnham to tackle 'mega-donors' in UK politics, minister says
News.content:
Reform has been critical of measures contained in the bill and the impact they could have on funding the party receives from donors.

There are currently no restrictions on the amount of money UK-based donors can give to political parties and politicians.

Labour MP Stella Creasy said donations from individuals and companies giving Â£1m or more had "surged" in the last decade and gave examples for different political parties.

Among those she named was British billionaire Christopher Harborne, a Thailand-based businessman, who is one of Reform's biggest backers.

Last year he gave a single donation of Â£9m to Reform - the biggest single donation to a UK political party by a living person.

Creasy was among those who tabled amendments seeking to also impose a cap on UK-based donors.

One of her proposals called for an immediate Â£500,000 limit which would reduce to Â£100,000 in the second calendar year. Minsters would have been able to set a permanent cap.

The amendment, which was not moved to a vote, was signed by more than 60 MPs.

Creasy told the Commons: "Obscene wealth is increasingly dictating who is heard, whether we like it or not, what issues are being prioritised and whose interests shape policy decisions."

The Walthamstow MP added that there was a "need to act now to protect the next general election". Her proposals would have exempted trade unions from the donation cap, with the MP saying this is "already well regulated" and "clean money".

Kruger highlighted the millions of pounds donated by trade unions to the Labour Party as he criticised the proposals and the bill.

The MP for East Wiltshire said: "The claim is made that this bill will defend democracy, but actually it's a flagrantly partisan attempt to kneecap Reform UK."

The former Conservative MP added: "The suggestion is made that this bill will restore trust in politics and that is exactly what is needed.

"But what they all mean is to restore trust in the class of politicians and in the political parties that have got us into the mess that we are in, including the party I'm afraid to say I was part of which is why I left it. We need change."

Responding for the government, Eshalomi said the bill "already contains a package of significant measures designed to strengthen the political finance regime whilst ensuring that legitimate donors can continue to fund election campaigns".

The communities minister added that the prime minister was among those "determined to tackle the UK-based issue of mega-donors in UK politics".

"That is why I'm happy to commit and announce the new cross-government task and finish team will be working at pace to find a solution without unintended consequences," Eshalomi said.

"I can reassure members that once these solutions have been found, we would want them in force as soon as possible."

Full details of the new team's remit have yet to be confirmed by the government.

It last month emerged that Burnham registered accepting Â£345,000 of donations over the past year, including Â£164,347 from businessman Lord Sainsbury.

The Liberal Democrats proposed establishing a royal commission to make recommendations for a cap on political donations and the "effectiveness" of existing campaign expenditure limits.

This proposal was rejected in the Commons by 427 votes to 85, majority 342.

Green Party MP Ellie Chowns said Creasy had made a "clear case" for a cap on all donations, adding she would prefer it to be lower and suggested Â£50,000 a year.

Conservative shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said it was a "noble aim" to protect UK democracy from foreign influence but changes proposed by the government had not always been produced with "proper care and attention".

In March, the government said donations in cryptocurrency to UK political parties would be banned alongside the move to cap donations of British citizens living abroad at Â£100,000 annually.

Ministers later announced overseas voters moving to the UK would be prevented from giving more than Â£100,000 in political donations for a year after their arrival.

This was announced alongside tougher checks on company donations, which they believe will help stop foreign money from influencing UK elections.

The bill also contains measures to change the voting system, including extending the right to vote to 16- and 17-year-olds.

MPs approved the bill at third reading by 411 votes to 102, majority 309, and it will undergo further scrutiny in the House of Lords at a later date.

News.title: Petrol bomber jailed over attack on family home
News.content:
A man has been jailed for more than six years after he threw a petrol bomb at a house in Rotherham.

Seven people were in the property in Warwick Street, in Moorgate, at the time of attack in November 2023, including two children and an 11-month-old baby.

South Yorkshire Police said six people had managed to get out of the house unharmed, while one occupant suffered serious leg injuries from having to jump out of a window.

Jamal Usman, 23, of no fixed abode, plead guilty to arson being reckless as to whether life is endangered at Sheffield Crown Court on Friday and was sentenced to six years and four months. He was told he would serve an additional three years on licence after being released.

A police spokesperson said officers were called to reports of a fire in the early hours of 25 November 2023.

CCTV later showed a group of people, including Jamal Usman, arrive nearby in a taxi before throwing a petrol bomb at the property.

Two people are still wanted in relation to the offence.

Det Sgt Chris Byne said it was "frankly a miracle that no lives were lost".

"I want to praise the victims in this case who have supported our investigation from the outset, their bravery and determination to see justice served a big role in this result," he said.

"Usman showed a shocking lack of humanity, having a complete and utter disregard for the safety of those inside the house he targeted.

"It was only from the help of neighbours who attended with ladders that the occupants managed to escape."

News.title: Orange Order submits new 'limited' Drumcree parade plans
News.content:
Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson said they had "lodged a notification to complete our return church parade, which we have been unlawfully and unjustly denied since 1998, and to bring our bannerette home to Carleton Street Orange Hall for the first time in just under 30 years".

He said the current Parades Commission should not be making the final determination on the submission, as a result of the recent court case.

"That this commission remains in office, particularly the chair, is an affront to good public administration and undermines the authority of the secretary of state, who has shown himself impotent in the face of belligerent and arrogant commission," he said.

"Let us be very clear: they have no credibility, they have no legitimacy and they have no lawful right to play any role in this determination."

He added that there was no threat of violence or disruption from "any section of our community" regardless of the outcome of the application.

Portadown deputy district master Alistair Power said: "This limited parade is proportionate, inoffensive and wholly reasonable.

After the court case, there were calls for the resignation of the commissioners, including the chair, Prof Evelyn Collins. One commissioner Billy Gamble, who had faced the most public criticism, resigned.

The five-member Parades Commission now has 24 days to make a decision.

They will consult widely before announcing their verdict.

The commissioners' jobs are part-time but their deliberations will be long and intensive.

The deadline for a decision is Sunday 27 September but it is likely to come a few days beforehand.

Anyone who disagrees with their judgement has the right to seek a judicial review of the decision.

A judge-led review into the Parades Commission is due to begin this month, instructed by the Secretary of State, Chris Bryant, and it will be completed before the end of November.

Dessie is a resident on the Garvaghy Road and and said the Orange Order is "marching over our rights".

Speaking to The Nolan Show, Dessie said there "should be no parade ever" on the Garvaghy Road.

"No more weekly determinations so we can live as a community," he added.

Posting on social media, external, the First Minister, Michelle O'Neill, said: "The days of unwanted marches being imposed on the Garvaghy Road community are over.

"The people of this small community should be left to live in peace, free from fear and intimidation," she added.

O'Neill said her party "stands fully with the people of Garvaghy Road".

News.title: Alan Carr lodges plans to turn castle potting shed into café
News.content:
Comedian Alan Carr has lodged plans to convert a potting shed at his castle in the Scottish Borders into a cafe and estate shop.

The Celebrity Traitors winner bought 19th Century Ayton Castle earlier this year.

A new TV series is planned following his attempt to turn the ageing estate into a workable home.

Now he has put in a planning application to Scottish Borders Council (SBC) to redevelop a part of the estate.

News.title: Michael Sheen says Wales should be asked if it wants the Prince of Wales title back
News.content:
Welsh people should be asked whether they want to take the Prince of Wales title back when it next becomes vacant, believes Michael Sheen.

The actor said the title, currently held by Prince William, "symbolises something that was essentially a put-down to Wales".

"Obviously that was a long, long time ago, but these things have power still," he added.

The Hollywood actor was speaking ahead of his forthcoming portrayal of Owain GlyndÅµr, the last Welsh-born Prince of Wales, in a new theatre production at the Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff.

Kensington Palace declined to comment.

The Royal Family reserves the Prince of Wales title for the heir apparent to the British throne, in a centuries-old tradition.

William and his wife Catherine, the current Princess of Wales, were given the titles by King Charles III following the death of Queen Elizabeth in 2022.

News.title: Kirstie Allsopp airlifted to hospital after fall during birthday celebrations
News.content:
TV presenter Kirstie Allsopp has revealed she was airlifted to hospital for surgery after slipping and injuring her leg while walking home from a beach in Devon on holiday.

The Location, Location, Location host, 55, shared a photo on Instagram, external of her lying in an ambulance with cuts on her face and a breathing tube up her nose.

She explained in the adjoining caption how she had "slipped on a muddy patch on the steep path", while walking back with her family following her birthday celebrations.

"We have a picnic on the beach at Welcombe Mouth, a swim and a walk back to the house for some cake," she wrote of the longstanding family tradition.

It took "a whole host of people to get me to hospital", she added.

"After a little wait while poor Oscar [her son, 18] ran as fast as he could to get help, and the RNLI Bude Lifeboat paramedics and Cornwall Air Ambulance tracked me down."

She then asked for help identifying those who had helped her, noting how she had been given "a huge amount of painkillers" so was "high as a kite!"

"Everyone at Barnstaple hospital has been amazing, kind and caring, so many lovely people doing their absolute best."

News.title: Tributes paid to 107-year-old WW2 veteran who has died
News.content:
Tributes have been paid to World War Two veteran Norman Irwin, from Coleraine, who has died at the age of 107.

The death of Norman Irwin was announced by his family on Thursday.

Norman Irwin, who was born in 1918 and was understood to be Northern Ireland's oldest living person before his passing, served in eight countries during WW2 and played a vital role in protecting the Suez Canal from German attacks.

In 2025, he was awarded a British Empire Medal (BEM) for a range of voluntary work in his County Londonderry hometown, including at a cross-community club for retirees.

Donald Trump has labelled Iran’s strikes on US targets as a “love tap” after US forces had hit the country “very hard” in yet another bizarre rant.

Iranians, Europeans, and others in the region fear a return of the conflict in earnest after the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington since July took place on Wednesday.

“It was a very heavy attack last night, and we’re prepared to do another one anytime we want,” Trump said on Wednesday according to Fox News.

“We have technology that's incredible. Nobody has technology like we have. So, we hit them hard last night, very hard. They gave a little love tap, but we hit them very hard.”

It comes amid fears Trump is planning to extend Washington’s war on Iran, after The Wall Street Journal reported that the Pentagon was extending the presence of troops in the Middle East into next year.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is quietly stretching the presence of troops in the region as part of an strategy to leave Trump with open-ended options in the war, sources told the outlet.

Trump said the US is prepared to launch another attack at “any time”, but added that a renewed campaign would not last “too long”.

Donald Trump has suggested he would not back Britain if Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands as the row over its sovereignty deepens.

Asked if he would come to the aid of the UK in the event of another invasion, Mr Trump appeared to hit out again at what he sees as a failure to support his war in Iran.

He told GB News: “Your country was not there to help me.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump made a jibe at the UK, saying: ‘You weren’t there for me’ ( AFP/Getty )

His comments come after he suggested on Monday that he was reviewing the United States’ position on British sovereignty over the archipelago.

The next day, Argentina’s president – a close ally or Mr Trump – issued a fresh warning to the UK over the islands, saying his country would defend its interests “with tooth and nail, no matter who it bothers”.

Javier Milei said he would make a national announcement on Thursday night, adding the islands were “sacred” and his country’s national sovereignty had been “violated”.

No 10 insists the UK’s position on the Falklands is “long-standing and unwavering”.

Falkland Islanders voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory in a 2013 referendum, with 99.8 per cent voting in favour – and just three votes against.

Asked in an interview with GB News today whether he would “come to the aid” of the UK in the event of another invasion, Mr Trump said he clearly remembered the 1982 war.

“I was there when they had the first war, that was a long time ago... you comported yourself very well, took it back very shortly. But it is a long way away,' he said.

“So, your country's not doing well. Don't forget you get a big percentage of your oil from the Strait of Hormuz and you weren't there to help me. Your country was not there to help me.”

open image in gallery Argentina’s president Javier Milei has said he is preparing to make a national announcement on Thursday night, saying the islands were “sacred” to his people and claimed his country’s national sovereignty had been “violated” . ( Reuters )

The UK initially refused to take part in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran, when Keir Starmer was PM.

He later agreed to support “defensive” strikes against targets such as missile launchers, but did not back Mr Trump's call to send the Navy to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

In response, Mr Trump repeatedly hit out at Sir Keir, branding him at one point “no Churchill”.

In a statement on X, formerly Twitter, on Wednesday, Argentina’s president wrote: “We announce a national broadcast for Thursday at 9:00 PM on a SACRED topic for Argentinians... a historic claim of the Argentine people that to this day continues to see its national sovereignty violated.”

He added: “What more important and strategic cause for the vital interests of the nation could there be more important than the Malvinas cause?... We will continue defending the interests of the Argentine nation with tooth and nail, no matter who it bothers. LONG LIVE FREEDOM, DAMMIT...!!!”

The issue hit the headlines this summer when Argentina’s football team controversially waved a banner in support of their country’s claim to the islands while celebrating their World Cup win against England. Players held a banner after the semi-final match that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates as “The Falklands are Argentine”.

This is a breaking news story, more follows

Katie Taylor finished preparation for her Croke Park farewell against the unbeaten Flora Pili by inviting a young fan into the ring to train with her.

Once Taylor had completed her session at Wednesday’s open workout, she picked out Clodagh Keating from the crowd at random, gloved up her right hand and then coached her to throw some shots while moving.

Keating, a 10-year-old aspiring boxer from Dublin who has been learning the basics in classes, burst into tears at the prospect of being in the ring with her idol and then had her hand held aloft when the session was over.

Taylor is aiming to become a three-time undisputed world champion by defeating Pili with a sold-out 80,000 crowd in attendance for her final fight before retiring.

open image in gallery Katie Taylor with a young fan Clodagh Keating, aged 10, during an open workout ( Brian Lawless/PA )

Speaking at the ticketed event at The Helix in Dublin, Taylor said: “Just feeling the atmosphere in this small arena, I can’t imagine what Saturday evening is going to be like.

“This is what it’s all about for me. It’s just an absolute joy to be here. I’m so grateful for what I get to do. I actually love every single day and I don’t take this for granted.

“In a few days I’ll make my last ring walk and I’ll look back on this in a few years and I imagine I’ll be overwhelmed.”

The Olympic gold medallist continued: “For the last few months I’ve been training to give my career best performance, purely for everyone’s support over these last few years.

“The last 30 years of my whole career, you guys have been with me from the start. You were with me throughout the London 2012 Olympics, you were with me through the heartbreak of Rio and then you stayed with me when I turned pro. I’m so grateful, thank you so much.”

Taylor turned 40 early last month but the ‘Bray Bomber’, who has posted 25 wins in 26 fights, is ready for what will be the most cherished moment of her career.

She said: “I feel great. I think 40 is the new 30 or something! I actually just turned 40 a few weeks ago, but I feel great – thank God.

“I’m obviously expecting a tough fight, but this is what I’m made for, this what I’m born for. I love the tough challenges. I love the tough fights.

News.title: Two mice face off in front of amused commuters at London Underground
News.content:
Two mice were caught on camera fighting on a platform at a London Underground station.

Footage shared by Sonia Mansfield on Saturday (29 August) shows the pair of rodents sparring in front of passengers at Oxford Circus station.

It was a scene similar to that in a photograph that won the Wildlife Photographer of the Year people's choice award in 2019.

Sam Rowley's "Station squabble" shows two mice fighting over scraps of food, before one grabbed a crumb and they went their separate ways.

A newborn baby was found alive in a sanitary bin in a toilet at an international airport in Malaysia, leading to the arrest of a man and a woman.

Police arrested a 23-year-old Malaysian woman and a 22-year-old man from Myanmar in connection with the case, according to South-West district police chief Anuwal Ab Wahab.

The baby was found by a member of the cleaning staff after they heard cries coming from a sanitary bin in a toilet designated for people with disabilities on Monday.

The baby was taken to hospital for treatment, Mr Wahab said, adding that an investigation had been launched.

Police reviewed CCTV footage from the airport, which led to the woman’s arrest at Bukit Jambul Complex, a shopping mall near Penang International Airport, Mr Anuwal said on Tuesday.

“Further investigations led to the arrest of a 22-year-old Myanmar national who works as a security guard,” he said.

The man was detained to assist with the investigation and was also found to be unable to produce valid travel documents, he added.

( Getty/iStock )

The case is being investigated under laws relating to the abandonment of a child under 12 by a parent or person having care of the child.

“Further investigations are ongoing to determine the involvement of and connection between the individuals detained and the incident,” Mr Wahab said.

According to Free Malaysia Today, the baby appeared to have been abandoned shortly after birth, as the placenta and umbilical cord were still attached to the baby.

A video showing the baby inside the bin has since gone viral on Malaysian social media.

The incident is a reminder of a grim 2016 incident in which a newborn baby boy was found dead inside a sanitary bin in a toilet at Tampines MRT station in Singapore.

A cleaner discovered the baby in a red plastic bag. The case later went before a coroner, who recorded an open verdict because the cause of death could not be established. Investigators linked three Indonesian women to the abandonment, with one believed to be the mother.

At least 80 people are feared dead after a boat that had been adrift for 26 days was discovered off Spain’s Canary Islands, an NGO has said.

Four women and a baby are feared to be among those who died on a small boat that departed Gambia on 7 August, and was discovered following an alert raised by Spanish NGO Caminando Fronteras, the organisation told The Independent.

Spain’s news agency EFE Noticias initially reported on X that 80 migrants had been found dead on the boat. Maritime Rescue afterwards told The Independent that 44 people and five bodies were found onboard at 6:40pm on Wednesday, three of whom were airlifted to hospital.

Caminando Fronteras said the boat had initially been carrying 127 people, with more than 80 declared to be dead or missing.

“Throughout this period, as you can imagine, numerous family members were calling in desperation, fearing the worst; ultimately, the tragedy has been confirmed,” the spokesperson for Caminendo Fronteras added. “We are talking about more than 80 victims.”

“Once again, we must question the level of cooperation between the search-and-rescue services of various countries, as well as the search resources available for these vessels that end up adrift and clearly require urgent rescue.”

Survivors on the boat, which was brought to the port of Arguineguin in Gran Canaria, reportedly told the Red Cross they had left for the Canary Islands with more than 100 people on board.

It comes one day after the Moroccan navy intercepted 201 migrants attempting to reach Spain’s Canary Islands after departing from Western Sahara, according to Info Migrants. The boat was intercepted 185 kilometres (115 miles) southwest of Dakhla, according to the Moroccan general staff, EFE.

According to The Times, maritime rescue said the vessels was first spotted on Wednesday afternoon. Spanish search and rescue vessel the Guardamar Urania provided help at midnight, it said.

All the survivors are reportedly from Gambia and Mali, the outlet added.

The Independent has contacted the Maritime Rescue and Guardia Civil.

The western Africa to Canary Islands migrant route has become one of the world’s most deadly in recent years, with lives lost rising by 480 per cent between 2019 and 2025 (202 to 1,172), according to the Missing Migrants Project.

“We’re seeing that, because the counter-smuggling enforcement on a lot of the West and North African departure countries is getting stricter, people are leaving from as far south as the Gambia, an overseas journey of weeks, which is crazy when it’s often a fishing boat,” a spokesperson for the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), which runs the MMP, previously told The Independent.

In 2026, 349 people have died so far, according to MMP figures. This is not believed to include the 80 who have reportedly been found dead near the Canary Islands.

The route is by far the deadliest migration route from Africa, MMP figures show.

GoPro has been bought – and it appears to be turning into something very different.

The company is best known for its action cameras, and the dramatic footage of extreme sports and other dramatic incidents that they have been able to capture. But in recent years it has struggled, with declining sales in large part because of an improvement in smartphone cameras.

Now, it will merge with tech company Starman Optical and seems to be attempting to focus on other, potentially more controversial products.

While it will continue to support its existing products, it will also move towards a “broader, diversified product roadmap”, the company said in a statement announcing the merger.

That will include using its cameras for “defence, government, robotics and aerospace”, it said, which suggests that the same technology could soon be put to military use.

GoPro had already said in April that it was exploring “new market opportunities for its technology within the defence and aerospace sector” as an attempt to solve its financial problems, though it gave few details on what form that might take.

GoPro will merge with tech company Starman Optical ( Reuters )

“Advanced optics and imaging are essential to AI, national security, and the broader economy,” Starman chief executive Charles Tebele said.

Mr Tebele’s statement stressed the fact that much of that technology is made overseas, and that the merger would help allow those military capabilities to be manufactured in the United States.

Similarly, GoPro founder and chief executive Nicholas Woodman said that the merger would allow GoPro to “grow across consumer, commercial and defense markets as a leading American imaging and optical solutions company, addressing important areas of national security related to cameras, optics and AI infrastructure”.

Starman makes optical transceivers, which are used to turn electrical signals into light pulses and vice versa. Those products will be added to GoPro’s portfolio.

The merger comes just days after it emerged that Mark Fischbach, the YouTuber known as Markiplier, had acquired a 8.5 per cent stake in the company, valued at $9 million.

That had already provoked some controversy of its own, after he posted a video about the company’s cameras without disclosing his relationship with it.

News.title: Ted Cruz sounding out staffers for potential 2028 presidential run: report
News.content:

Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz has reportedly begun sounding out potential staffers to work on his 2028 presidential campaign as the GOP starts squaring up to the prospect of a post-Donald Trump future.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Cruz, 55, “is already putting in the legwork in Iowa, hitting the podcast circuit and embarking on a book tour,” all omens foreshadowing a likely run.

It adds: “He is also quietly asking people if they would be interested in working on his 2028 bid, according to people familiar with the requests.”

The Independent has reached out to Cruz’s office for comment.

Vice President JD Vance is widely seen as the president’s natural successor, is well ahead in early polling and appears to have Trump’s backing, with the president reportedly telling Republican donors at a recent private dinner: “At the end of the day, we need to elect JD.”

open image in gallery Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz is being tipped to make a 2028 presidential run ( Getty )

That came after months of Trump asking conservatives who they would prefer as their next nominee out of Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, pitting the two men against each other, with the latter politely indicating he would not run as a challenger to the VP.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth apparently has no such qualms and is said to be mulling his own bid for the White House, discussing it with friends and associates, according to NBC News.

The VP has yet to confirm his intention to run, focusing for now on the midterms, and could yet choose to opt out, given that his wife Usha Vance has just given birth to their fourth child and the likelihood of Democrats enjoying a bounce in the polls in reaction to Trump.

However, the Journal cites Vance allies who “dismissed and scoffed at” the prospect of Cruz providing the opposition to his potential candidacy, “arguing he wouldn’t be a serious threat.”

Former Trump strategist Steve Bannon was also dismissive of the senator, commenting: “He’s going to have plenty of money, but unfortunately he’s not a populist, he’s a throwback to the neocon and neoliberal policies of the old Republican Party that’s essentially been destroyed.”

open image in gallery Vice President JD Vance would appear to be in pole position for the GOP nomination and his allies have said they see no ‘serious threat’ from Cruz ( Getty )

Cruz has not been afraid to attack Vance, saying on a recent podcast appearance that the VP’s memorandum of understanding with Iran, attempting to bring an end to the ongoing war, had been “a terrible deal.”

He also addressed the importance of gaining Trump’s endorsement, while preparing the ground for his not receiving it, by saying: “It carries weight, but I think the voters are going to make their own determination.”

Cruz rose to prominence during the Tea Party era and ran against Trump for the GOP nomination in 2016, a bad-tempered race in which the ultimate winner nicknamed him “Lyin’ Ted,” alleged that his father Rafael had been involved in the assassination of John F Kennedy and publicly insulted his wife Heidi.

The senator has since enjoyed a much friendlier relationship with the president, who promoted his new book on Truth Social this week, and even excused Trump’s insults a decade ago as “political genius.”

Perhaps a bigger obstacle for Cruz is his propensity for gaffes, which have been frequent and met with glee by online commentators.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has enjoyed pitting Vance against other Cabinet members but recently told donors they should support his VP’s candidacy ( Reuters )

The senator’s official account notoriously liked a two-minute clip from an adult film that was posted on Twitter by “SexuallPosts” in September 2017, a blunder subsequently blamed on an unnamed staffer.

Cruz was also roasted for going on vacation to Cancun while his state was suffering a power and water crisis in February 2021, for spending more time on his podcast than legislating and for being unable to answer Tucker Carlson’s elementary questions about Iran while lobbying for greater U.S. military aggression against its theocratic regime.

Most recently, he has been laughed at for warning against billionaire presidents who “steal and rob from those they govern,” attacked for spreading misinformation wrongly linking the Covid-19 vaccine to miscarriages and forced to take down a tribute to the late Dolly Parton when the account he reposted changed its username to belittle him.

News.title: Burnham risks Truss moment, warn bond traders
News.content:
Andy Burnham risks a Liz Truss-style market meltdown unless he presents a credible plan to pay for his agenda, bond traders have warned.

Investors said the Prime Minister faces further spikes in borrowing costs unless he outlines tax rises or spending cuts to fund his major policies.

UK borrowing costs have surged to multi-decade highs this week amid a global bond market sell-off. However, investors are particularly concerned about Mr Burnham’s fiscal agenda before his first Budget next month.

Al Cattermole, a portfolio manager at Swiss private bank Mirabaud, said investors were “unclear” about the Prime Minister’s plans and how he would pay for them.

He said: “If you have a lack of credibility about your spending plan and how that will be funded, then you would get spikes in yields similar to [what] we saw during the Liz Truss episode.

“That was about unfunded fiscal spending. And if you get that again, then there is concern about that.”

Mr Burnham refused to rule out increasing borrowing during his first Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday despite recent market turmoil.

Jim Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment, said: “Spending cuts are the thing the market wants to hear.

“It would go a long way if this Government were to recognise that it is a challenge that needs addressing – that the path we are on in terms of welfare spending is completely unsustainable.”

He added: “The market knows that, and the market wants to hear that the Government understands that.”

Lord Jim O’Neill said earlier that the Prime Minister must “get real” and cut public spending in order to ease pressure in the bond market.

The cost of long-term government borrowing hit its highest level since 1998 on Wednesday, increasing the strain on the public finances as John Healey, the new Chancellor, prepares for the Budget.

The 10-year gilt yield – a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money – has risen to its highest point since 2007.

News.title: H5N1 hits US mink farms, sparking calls for an urgent cull
News.content:
H5N1 has been detected on a US mink farm for the first time, igniting fears the infected animals could present a human pandemic risk.

The bird flu virus, which has “jumped” from birds to numerous mammal species and infected hundreds of people in recent years, was detected in at least six mink on a farm in Utah in mid-August, according to a notification from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) released over the weekend.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms gives invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate. Mink also have strikingly similar respiratory systems to humans, which greatly increases the human risk.

The animals are farmed for their fur, which is then typically exported to fashion manufacturers in China, Hong Kong, and Russia and used in items like coats and scarves.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 acquires the ability to spread efficiently between people, it could trigger a human pandemic.

“Avian influenza viruses tend to replicate pretty poorly in humans and don’t really have the right sort of properties that allow them to transmit from person to person.

“If H5N1 were to cause a pandemic, it would need to make quite a lot of changes, and there’s a real concern that mink, particularly farmed mink, have a lot of the features that could drive the evolution of H5N1,” Dr Tom Peacock, a virologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

News.title: Collapsing child vaccination in South Africa ‘a public health emergency’
News.content:
Plummeting child immunisation rates are now a public health emergency in South Africa and risk causing outbreaks of preventable but potentially deadly childhood diseases, the government has said.

The proportion of children under one who have received no vaccinations has trebled in the past decade to nearly a third of infants in South Africa.

Mistrust of vaccines and growing ignorance about the benefits of childhood immunisations risk undoing years of progress made by one of the continent’s most effective health systems.

Outbreaks of measles, diphtheria and whooping cough this year have all been linked to poor immunisation rates and are evidence that herd immunity is breaking down, officials warned.

An alert from the department for health said the proportion of unvaccinated infants had hit 36.3 per cent in the first four months of 2026, up from 12.1 per cent in 2017.

The department warned the jump was “effectively tripling the number of completely unvaccinated children and leaving hundreds of thousands of infants at risk of life-threatening illnesses”.

Coverage of the six-in-one hexavalent infant vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, meningitis, and hepatitis B declined from 87 per cent to 60.5 per cent over the same period.

Officials said the shortfall was caused by a lack of people coming forward to bring their children for jabs and was not due to any shortage of vaccines.

Dr Nonhlanhla Ndlovu, deputy director general of South Africa’s health department, told the state broadcaster that parents had a poor understanding of the public health benefits of childhood jabs.

She said: “The second one that comes out is the issue of public trust, in terms of the safety of the vaccines, but also the trust in terms of our systems.”

“Theses vaccines are very safe and we have seen the gains that we have had in our years before and now that is changing.

“The benefit of vaccines far outweigh anything we can talk about in public health. We need them to come back and bring the children for immunisation.”

News.title: Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer
News.content:
It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Julian Alvarez to Barcelona… or Arsenal

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Lamine Camara to Chelsea

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

The relentless transfer guru is one of the football world’s best-known sources of transfer information.

Sports.title: Lioness legend Millie Bright reveals she is pregnant and set to welcome first child with influencer boyfriend
Sports.content:
LIONESS legend Millie Bright has revealed pregnant with her first child!

The stunning footballer and her influencer boyfriend have revealed they’re set to welcome their first child together, five months after beginning their romance.



Millie’s partner Tom Mitchell is a TikTok star with a substantial following on all platforms.

The influencer, who owns his own hair salon in Sheffield, has over 200k Instagram followers and nearly 300k on TikTok.



Announcing the baby news during an interview with Women’s Health, the pair – who have recently moved in together – said they’re over the moon to welcome a little one.

“It’s overwhelming, it’s exciting to bring another life into the world,” the footballer said in the announcement, as her other half admitted he was “very surprised” when she told him the news.



But it’s not been without its challenges, said Millie, who is getting used to the changes in her body.

“It’s been difficult. I’m used to being very athletic and my body fitting into certain clothes, and that’s been changing.



“Now I’m embracing it and I feel good about myself, confident and happy, because I’m getting to the stage where I look pregnant and feel pregnant, whereas before I just felt unfit.”

The sportswoman also explained that she has struggled with morning sickness and found it tough to “keep food down” during the first trimester.

Back in April, Tom confirmed that he was in a relationship with Millie.

Tom took to social media to share a loved up snap and wrote: “Started off as content.

“Things happen quick and people click (like never before)… first weekend as my partner and couldn’t be happier or prouder to be with you.



“Just the start!! Plenty of memories to be come and definitely made a HUGE difference to my life in such a short amount of time!

“Thank you Millie Bright had the BEST weekend, so glad I’ve met you.”

Millie gushed in the comment section: “Special human. Haven’t stopped belly laughing, so many things to come T. Feeling extremely lucky. MAD MAD MAD. Don’t ever change.”

One photo showed Millie kissing Tom’s cheek and another snap of her bracing her head on his shoulder.

Other pictures included them in their dressing gown cooking and enjoying a takeaway pizza.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes after The Sun revealed last June that Millie had left fiancé Levi Crew and fallen for a married personal trainer and dad-of-seven Dave Zetolofsky.

But we then shared in December that Millie and Dave had “grown apart” and the latter moved out of her Surrey house.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney blocked entire Man Utd team from leaving plane in furious stand-off while stood in pyjama bottoms
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY was so fuming about being pranked on a plane that he blocked the entire Manchester United team from getting off.

Even Sir Alex Ferguson and club icon Sir Bobby Charlton were forced to sit tight while Wazza had it out with his team-mates.



United stars got one over on Rooney by hiding his suit trousers and playing dumb over where they had gone.

The ex-England star responded by marching to the front of the plane and sticking it on the entire team.



Pointing to former team-mate Wes Brown on Stick to United, Rooney recalled: “I knew these would s*** themselves and give me them back.

“I had my pyjama bottoms on, a shirt, a tie and a blazer.

“As soon as the plane landed I went straight to the front.

“The manager’s there, Bobby Charlton’s there. I’ve said, ‘Sorry boss, no one is getting off this plane until I get my bottoms back’. He didn’t know what to do.

“Eventually they s*** themselves and the pants started to get passed down. Otherwise they wouldn’t have.

“I wasn’t walking through the airport like that.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Brown, who played for United between 1996 and 2011, labelled it one of hot-headed Rooney’s biggest blow-ups.

And he chimed in: “We got the reaction we wanted. Happy days.”

Sports.title: Mo Salah flies back to UK as wife Magi welcomes baby boy and sister shares adorable name
Sports.content:
MO SALAH is back in the UK after his wife Magi gave birth to their son.

Salah, 34, left Liverpool and the Premier League to join Turkish side Trabzonspor at the end of last season after nine years at Anfield.



But it took him just months to make his return as he joined his wife for the birth of their third child.

His sister Rabab revealed on social media that the couple had welcomed a son, who was reportedly born in Liverpool.



She also revealed the child’s name, Leil.

The name translates to “night” in Arabic.

Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan also confirmed the birth of the child, via 61saat.

He even revealed that Salah was apparently not the only big Premier League name at the club who was jetting back for the birth of their child.

He said: After the (Amed SK) match, I travelled abroad with Salah and Andre Onana.

“Both of them had new children, Onana had twins and Salah a baby boy. I congratulate their families and their wives.”



Magi is the childhood sweetheart who grew up with Salah in their home town of Nagrig, and later trained as a biotechnician.

The pair, who married in 2013, also have two daughters.

Makka, their eldest, was born in 2014, while her sister Kayan arrived in 2020.

The birth is the latest update in a whirlwind few weeks for the Egyptian maestro.



He has started his career in Turkey with a bang, netting three goals in his opening three games for the side.

But that couldn’t stop manager Fatih Tekke from stepping down, despite Trabzonspor’s hopes to keep him on.

Sports.title: British NFL player Traore: I'll do what I need to do to make Dolphins impact
Sports.content:
You may have heard Seydou Traore's story before. The likelihood is that you'll hear it many more times throughout his NFL career.

Despite the recent successes of Jay Ajayi, Efe Obada and Jermaine Eluemunor, it is still rare to see a British player in the NFL, and Traore is already on a unique journey

By being selected in the 2026 NFL Draft (fifth round, 180th overall), Traore became the first player to have attended London's NFL Academy and later be drafted to the NFL - after taking part in trials as a 16-year-old at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium all the way back in 2019.

After moving to Florida to seek a college scholarship, he played two seasons at Arkansas State before transferring to Mississippi State, sitting out a year, then putting together two more seasons that caught the eyes of NFL scouts.

Since being drafted, he has made Miami's initial 53-man roster, but there is a lot more work to do. Traore spoke to Sky Sports this summer about the draft, landing in Miami, and his future in the league...

The NFL Draft experience

It was a long road from the NFL Academy to having his name called and walking across the stage in Pittsburgh, and Traore said the draft-day experience was "everything I expected and more".

He said: "Having my mum and my sister there with me meant a lot. Being able to reap the rewards of the years of hard work and the years they haven't been able to see me and be around me. As much as it was for me, it was for them.

"Heading on to that stage is an amazing feeling. I was speechless when I got out there, but yeah, it was amazing."

Unsurprisingly, Traore said he was inundated with "a bunch" of messages from people involved in the International Player Pathway programme, whether players, coaches or staff.

"Everyone from back home was checking up on me, congratulating me and just wishing me the best, saying they've either seen the videos or read this," he said.

"I was more than happy to go through each one and just connect with people and say thank you."

Life in Miami

Image: Traore faces a long road to make an NFL impact

After spending five years in what he called the "countryside" of Arkansas and Mississippi, Traore is back in a lively city.

However, he didn't have much time for exploring. First up was training, conditioning, film, playbook and importantly: forming connections.

The Dolphins are coming off a disappointing 7-10 season, their second straight losing campaign. That meant the end of the Mike McDaniel era and a fresh start in Miami.

For new head coach Jeff Hafley, new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, and new quarterback Malik Willis, the main goal is bringing the team together.

"The first thing is connection," Traore explained.

"Connection between the whole team and teammates and everything.

"We'll be eating; no one's on their phones. When they're in this building, people are trying to get better and connect with teammates.

Image: Traore played college football for Mississippi State

"So at the door, you understand once you get in here, you're coming in with a purpose.

"Everything outside, you can put on pause for a few hours, but get to know the people you're going to be with the whole day. Because those are the people that are going to have your back on the field."

What does the future hold?

Traore could offer something to a Miami team lacking offensive weapons right now, but it's a long road ahead.

Tight ends rarely make an instant impact, and fifth-round picks face a fight each and every year to make a team.

In his rookie campaign, his plan is "learning, soaking up as much as I can this first year and showing when I do have those chances, showing the ability to make a play."

Sports.title: Graffard's Drazinda faces Armor Supreme
Sports.content:
Lingfield, Southwell, Newcastle and ParisLongchamp are the venues for today's action - live on Sky Sports Racing.

2.40 ParisLongchamp - Listed winners Drazinda and Armor Supreme lock horns

Listed winners Drazinda and Armor Supreme lock horns in the Group three Prix d'Arenberg.

The Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Drazinda has improved with each run this season after a nice debut win. After chasing down Victorious and Senorita Bonita in the Queen Mary when drawn on the wrong side, she placed second in a Listed race before going one better last month.

A quality-looking edition of the Group 1 Prix Morny was a step too far, but this Sioux Nation filly still ran creditably and can continue her progression down in grade.

She just about sets the standard, although Diego Dias' progressive filly Armor Supreme beat the former in the Queen Mary when drawn on the quicker side. She then franked the form when scoring at Listed level impressively over at the Curragh last time out. She should be primed for a big run and these two should be closely matched.

Grayrobin won two on the bounce since moving to Kate McGivern before finishing just over a length behind the aforementioned Armor Supreme. She should go close again, albeit the winner was well on top at the line that day.

Archie Watson's Vollering and Valentina Bella round off the field of five, but both will need to improve a fair bit to feature at the front end.

4.55 Lingfield - Highly tried Kamaal drops in class against Mouj Albuhoor

On home soil, the highly-tried Kamaal drops in class against Arqana Series fifth Mouj Albuhoor in the Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 / EBF Novice Stakes.

Jack Jones' son of Minzaal sets a solid standard with an eye-catching 10th in the Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot. He then took a step backwards when eighth in the Rose Bowl but the ground may have been a touch too quick that day for a sharp six furlongs at Newbury. He shaped as if seven furlongs could suit when staying on at the Royal meeting and as a half-brother to Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf third North Coast, who ran his best at two over a mile, this lad can get back on track down in grade and up in trip.

The opposition is not without potential, with the Richard Hughes-trained Mouj Albuhoor clearly well thought of having gone off a short-priced favourite in the valuable Arqana Series Stakes at Deauville last month. He raced too freely to win that day but ran creditably in fifth and could be quite a nice type going forward.

The fourth-placed Munch came out and ran well in another novice, with seventh-placed Catch My Eye very much franking the form when improving markedly to beat promising juveniles Charged and Katon.

Ralph Beckett fields 125,000gns two-year-old Saturn Star, who contains more of a middle-distance-based pedigree. Any market clues will be informative for this debutant.

6.10 Southwell - Godolphin's Castlemont returns following striking debut success

Godolphin's Castlemont returns in the bettingsites.co.uk Novice Stakes following striking debut success.

A full-brother to Bay Bridge, Charlie Appleby's gelding put up a taking display when winning a fair novice at Windsor in July. He overcame inexperience when looking green a few furlongs out, but did his best work late to win with plenty in hand.

The step up in trip should only be an advantage judging by both pedigree and his debut performance, and he should prove tough to beat.

Walking On Stars is going the right way for Sir Mark Prescott and gets 12lbs from Billy Loughnane's aforementioned mount, whilst Maestro Del Mar and Liam Mera Kai set a fair standard with creditable runs this season. However, they will have to improve quite markedly to reach the level of Castlemont as long as the Godolphin contender runs to form.

Best of the rest...

At Lingfield, Hamdania bids to make it two from two Download The At The Races App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes but may need the run returning from a break. Andrew Balding's Mystic Music looks to be the best of the opposition, having chased home Moonswept at 50/1 the last day. Later on the card, Wyle Cop aims for a course and distance hat-trick in the Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap (4.20pm).

At Newcastle, Norfolk Stakes third Mussab looks to bounce back in the 3.59pm Admiral Race To Riches Novice Stakes having disappointed in the Gimcrack the last day. A step into calmer waters down in class should suit. Southwell's 5.05pm bettingsites.co.uk Novice Stakes sees the Amo-owned Black Orchid attempt to turn three seconds into a first success.

Back in France...

Impressive the last day at Dieppe, Daryoura seeks to back up that debut win against Juddmonte's Maintain and Prix de Diane fifth Evita in the Prix de Liancourt at ParisLongchamp. In the following Prix Joubert, Charlie Appleby's Ribbon Of Sea steps up in class, with stablemate Tribal Queen also in situ.

Godspeed, Braida and Fortuna Diamond clash in the Prix de la Cochere (4.25pm), with representatives from the Jack Channon and James Fanshawe yards also present.

Sports.title: Norris reveals other 'opportunities' before committing future to McLaren
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has revealed he had other opportunities before signing a new contract to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030.

Norris, who has won the last two Formula 1 races, has been with McLaren since making his F1 debut in 2019 and says the contract was "probably the easiest contract I've had to sign".

The 26-year-old admitted though, in a wide-ranging interview with Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle which will air at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, that there were other options.

"There was opportunity of course. But opportunity that is positive. There's opportunities to gamble at times," he said.

"I'm a driver that personally I would take one or two tougher years over instant success - as I did a few years ago with McLaren.

"As much as I want to win every single year, not everything is about I need to be with a team tomorrow that's going to win the next race and do this and do that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Lando Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins

Norris pointed to the "strong" group of people at McLaren, led by team bosses Zak Brown and Andrea Stella, as a key reason to stay at the Woking-based outfit.

He added: "A good amount of it is also am I just happy? I was happy to be with McLaren even when we weren't winning because I'm still in an amazing opportunity and I still get to do the job I love and travel and do all these things. So not everything to me is about ultimate performance. A lot of it and a big part of it is the people that I'm with.

"Just the fact I feel I'm at home and I'm enjoying it. And that almost has enough control as saying 'I need to be with a team that is going to be performing and winning championships'."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater discusses the biggest talking points off the back of the Dutch Grand Prix, including if the championship chase is still on for Lando Norris

Would Norris ever join Ferrari?

Norris is currently in great form after claiming pole position and the win at the last two Grands Prix in Hungary and the Netherlands to cut his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points.

He has another good opportunity this Sunday as Antonelli will start at the back of the field due to grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation.

But, McLaren will still have the challenge of beating George Russell plus Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, who both have upgraded engines.

Hamilton and Leclerc will have huge support from the Tifosi at Monza, which features the most iconic podium as it overlooks the main straight and thousands of fans post-race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza.

Brundle pointed out Hamilton had previously stated he would stay at Mercedes before achieving his "dream" of joining Ferrari and asked if Norris would ever consider joining the Scuderia in the future.

The McLaren driver said: "That's not something I want to think about for now. Since I was a kid, you always think of yourself in different positions.

"My dream was always to be with McLaren. That's why I feel like I'm in a very fortunate position as I am. But you always want to experience the other side of things, whether that is Ferrari or other teams and Mercedes.

"It's just human. I think that you want to experience what it's like to be in this position and that position.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris sits down with Sky Sports' Rob Jones to discuss extending his stay with McLaren in a multi-year contract extension

"Also, the history of other teams. The fact Lewis also went to Mercedes from McLaren and then to Ferrari, I think it's also pretty cool that you try different things and you experience different stuff.

"It depends a little bit on what you want to achieve in your career. Do you want ultimate success every single year? Do you want to just experience what it's like to go to a different team and experience Ferrari or Mercedes?

"For now, I'll say I'm not thinking of it. But ask me again at the end of 2030."

Sports.title: Shields or Taylor the greatest? "We're 1A and 1B!"
Sports.content:
Claressa Shields has hailed the greatness of Katie Taylor and says she holds no qualms over a fight between the boxing greats never materialising.

Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans.

The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history.

Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Katie Taylor struggled to control her emotions as she discussed the privilege of finishing her illustrious career at Croke Park

"Am I number one? I have always shared that with Katie," Shields told Sky Sports. "Me and her joke and say we're 1A and 1B, because we're both just that good.

"I'm not a person that really cares about the pound for pound list. I know that I've been number one or two on there for the past five, six years.

"But I know that Katie, she's a great fighter. She's a warrior. And I wish her a happy retirement. And I hope that she gets a big knock out her last fight."

Shields, a three-time undisputed world champion, has fought at heavier weight-classes than Taylor, hence the pair never crossing paths in their respective glittering careers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chantelle Cameron says there's a 'very high possibility' of fighting Claressa Shields

"I'm not mad that it didn't happen," said Shields. "We had weight classes for a reason. And I respect her greatness and she respects mine.

"I beat the best in my divisions, and she's beat the best in her divisions. I respect that. So no, I'm not upset that we never got to fight.

"I am happy to be able to watch her and her greatness. She's done the same for me. And like I said, I wish her a happy retirement."

Taylor enters Saturday's contest 25-1 having suffered her only professional career defeat against Chantelle Cameron in May 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Amanda Serrano and Lucrecia Manzur. Credit: MVP

Among her highlights is a trilogy of wins over Puerto Rican great Amanda Serrano, the first of which saw the pair compete in the first ever women's boxing match to headline at Madison Square Garden.

"I think Katie's done what she wanted to do. I think this is her time," Serrano told Sky Sports.

"You can feel it, I've been 17 years in the sport. It's about time.

"Me and Katie, we've made lots of money together, we made history together and big fights. I think she's done enough for the sport. She deserves this homecoming fight.

"I'm happy for her. I just can't wait to see her future when she's retired with her family life and all that good stuff. She deserves it."

Sports.title: 'Think before you say stuff!' - Sabalenka fumes at preparation questions
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka cut short questions about her pre-tournament activities in an excruciating exchange with a reporter following her second-round win.

The two-time defending champion thrashed Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1 6-1 in 53 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

The Belarusian, who had faced a similar line of questioning ​after her first-round win, fired back that her off-court appearances had not come at the expense of her preparations ​for the Grand Slam.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aryna Sabalenka against Polina Iatchenko from the US Open

Sabalenka - a regular poster on social media at the various events she attends and with the brands she works with - replied: "You guys are, like, a joke.

"Parties, fun. Like, why would you even say that? Why would you even think about that? What kind of question is that?

"Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands, and you think that I've been partying, not training? The question, like, what is that?"

When the reporter responded: "I'm saying that there are a lot of events and things like that. I'm not saying you go to the parties," Sabalenka interrupted: "You literally said that. Next question."

The reporter replied: "For everyone who is unclear, I'm not suggesting that Aryna is having fun at these parties."

"Thanks, yeah," came the response.

"I'm saying that she makes a lot of appearances and there's a lot to do and lots of events, OK?" said the reporter.

"OK. Move on," replied Sabalenka.

She was then asked: "So, now that the tournament has started, do you find you're getting quite serious and combative?"

Sabalanka replied: "Oh, yeah, I wasn't serious before that. Next question. Think before you say stuff."

The world No 1, seeking a third straight ​title in New York to ‌emulate Serena Williams and Chris Evert, faces Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova on Friday looking for a 17th consecutive win at Flushing Meadows.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After her first-round win Sabalenka said she was tired of people's negativity towards her with everything she does both on and off the court

Carlos Alcaraz's comeback ‌from a long wrist injury layoff gathered momentum as ‌he came from behind to outclass Portugal's Jaime Faria ​4-6 6-0 6-3 6-2 and reach the third round.

The defending champion rebounded from an early deficit by winning eight straight games and beat Faria.

"After that I just tried to be focused, tried to stay calm and I'm thinking that good things are going to happen again," said Alcaraz, who is on a 16-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments.

Sports.title: Premier League paradox: midfielders are more and more expensive, yet more and more mediocre | Jonathan Liew
Sports.content:
Perhaps the only thing you really need to know about the modern midfield role is that Enzo Maresca reckons that Marc Guéhi can play it better than Mateo Kovacic. Guéhi, in reality a centre-back, started the season in midfield for Manchester City, ahead of Kovacic, the now-departed Nico González, and Matheus Nunes. In this context City’s purchase of Enzo Fernández for a club record £125m can be seen in one of two ways: either an enormous statement of intent, or a hell of a lot of money to pay for Guéhi’s understudy.

We jest, of course. Fernández is in fact a very different kind of midfielder to Guéhi, largely on the basis that he actually is a midfielder. Versatile, able to receive deep from the goalkeeper or the centre-halves; capable of recycling or progressing the ball in tight spots, driving into final-third positions as a No 8, ghosting into the penalty area and offering an advanced goal threat.
