Furiously speaking out on the failed transfers on Wednesday morning, Kamara posted on his Instagram story: 'The cases of Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara must all interrogate us.

'We have to get out of this logic where the African player can sometimes give the feeling that he is just a commodity: you buy it, you set its price, you negotiate its future and, too often, your will seems to go to the background.

'Our African players deserve respect. The respect of their work. The respect of their career. Respecting their ambitions. The respect of their voices.

The agent of Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr (left) and Monaco's Lamine Camara (right) has launched a scathing attack on clubs after his players failed to secure a move on deadline day

Agent Diomansy Kamara has accused clubs of treating African players as 'just a commodity'

'A transfer shouldn't just be a matter of two clubs and numbers. Behind every contract, there's a man, a career, dreams and life choices.

'The fact that clubs can sometimes have the final word is a reality of professional football. But one question remains: what about the career and the will of the player?

'The player must be able to be heard and respected in the decisions that determine his future.

'Let's never forget what's important: behind every success, it's the players who write history first.'

Camara's failed move to Chelsea became one of the main stories of deadline day as it left Xabi Alonso's side short in midfield following the British record departure of Enzo Fernandez for £125m to Manchester City.

Chelsea thought they had secured Camara from Monaco with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47m deal.

Yet, in a dramatic twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word as the 11pm deadline approached.

Chelsea sources say the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join. Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the deal for Camara was being withdrawn.

Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

Monaco's sporting director Thiago Scuro described the club's decision to pull out of the transfer as 'part of the game' in Wednesday's press conference.

Scuro revealed that Alonso had spoken to Camara, who had told Monaco he wanted to leave, but explained they pulled the plug after Balogun's move to Everton fell through.

According to the sporting director, wantaway Camara was told that Monaco would secure a major transfer for him 'very soon' and could present him with 'ever better options' than those that surfaced on deadline day.

He urged that Camara remains fully committed and professional with regards to his role at Monaco, despite feeling disappointed.

Sports.title: Inside Crystal Palace's transfer window: How Eagles held on to star duo, why they were happy to let Daniel Munoz go, how Brennan Johnson failure hurt business and what Dario Osorio and Quinten Timber bring to the table
Sports.content:
What was all the panic about? Crystal Palace may have left significant transfer business until after the window had officially closed but they can be content with their summer’s work.

Losing Daniel Munoz and Maxence Lacroix appeared a tricky inheritance for Pierre Sage, who already had the daunting task of succeeding Oliver Glasner, yet Palace – with recruitment led by Matt Hobbs, Iain Moody and chairman Steve Parish – eventually bolstered their squad after a late rush to Tuesday’s 11pm deadline.

Most importantly, Palace have kept Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr, much to the latter’s dismay. The talismanic pair – who scored 37 goals between them last term – both wanted to leave.

Sarr sulked while his agent kicked up a fuss. That was unsurprising, given one source told Daily Mail Sport over breakfast in June that his agent was keen to move him on. Palace remained resolute, though, refusing to sell the attacker with three years remaining on his contract.

Once the window closed, Sarr’s agent had his say, criticising the club for not executing the ‘will of the player’ – a strange comment given Sarr signed a five-year contract without a release clause just two years ago. The club had no obligation to sell him, particularly as he did not submit a transfer request.

But the question remains: how will he return? If Sarr wants to leave in January or next summer, the best way to make that happen is to apply himself and demonstrate why he deserves an upward move rather than continuing to sulk. After all, Palace have Europa League football and fancy their chances of a deep run in the competition.

Crystal Palace have managed to hang onto Ismaila Sarr (right) and Jean-Philippe Mateta

Pierre Sage has the daunting task of succeeding Oliver Glasner as Palace boss

There are no concerns about Mateta’s response. He will do what he did when his move to AC Milan collapsed in January: knuckle down and let the football do the talking once he has recovered from injury.

Holding on to attackers of their class is a triumph and Palace consolidated by adding depth, too. Dario Osorio, signed from Danish club Midtjylland, has plenty of upside as a winger who drifts inside, making him well suited to Sage’s 3-4-2-1 formation. The 22-year-old offers end product, talented ball delivery and averaged a goal or assist every 180 minutes last term.

Dwight McNeil is a curious addition, given he arrived in a straight swap for Brennan Johnson, whom Palace paid £30million for in January. Decision-makers accepted that they had got the Johnson transfer wrong, something a club with Palace's financial constraints cannot afford to do.

The swap did at least remove substantial money from the wage bill. But the Johnson overspend in January limited what Palace could do this summer, with the club finishing the window with a positive net spend as they sought to recoup some of the capital lost on their former record signing.

Evann Guessand has returned on loan following his stint at the club during the second half of last season. Before injury, he was a menace starting from the left and provided adequate back-up to Yeremy Pino.

Zavier Gozo was also signed in attack from Real Salt Lake, with the teenager viewed as one for the future. He came on against Manchester City last week and showed some exuberance. That is the type of business Palace should be doing: signing replacements for players years before their departure, providing them with the chance to learn from established players and adapt to the league before they are asked to fill in for them full time.

Last season, Palace ended the summer window with just four No 10s and wingers, with midfielders Daichi Kamada and Justin Devenny often required to fill in. This term, they have eight players to call upon for those spots. There is competition, alternatives and potential.

Replacing Lacroix with Axel Disasi is, admittedly, a downgrade. Lacroix started for France at the World Cup and is now Chelsea’s first-choice centre back. Disasi, meanwhile, is a Chelsea cast-off and nowhere near the France squad.

Decision-makers at Palace accept they had got the Brennan Johnson transfer wrong and he has been moved on to Everton

Axel Disasi has been brought in to beef up the Palace defence and adds experience

Lacroix held the Palace backline together with his recovery pace and immense physicality, qualities Palace will inevitably miss this season. Most importantly, though, he made Jaydee Canvot and Chris Richards better, guiding them through games.

Disasi may not have the same pace but he is experienced and a solid defender, though he can have his blips in possession. His arrival on loan at West Ham in January markedly improved their defence, helping them keep six clean sheets in 14 games.

Centre back remains the most concerning area. Canvot and Honest Ahanor, a deadline-day arrival from Atalanta, are promising but lack know-how. Ahanor is impressively imposing for his age, although it is a shame Palace are developing a player who will join Chelsea next summer – even if they have procured a skilled defender.

Richards is proven at right centre back but if Disasi becomes unavailable, he would have to move into the middle, where he has looked suspect. Oscar Mingueza, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Jefferson Lerma, who can all play in multiple positions, are viewed as understudies. Not adding another central centre back could be a costly omission as the backline appears fragile without Disasi.

Number-wise, though, it is an improvement. At one point last season, Palace had only four centre backs for three positions. They may lack a sprinkling of quality at the back but they have brought in enough depth to compete in Europe and domestically.

Losing Munoz to Glasner’s Nottingham Forest was emotionally tough for Palace, given the rivalry between the clubs and his role in winning three trophies in two years. But, from a business perspective, it was the right move.

Munoz, now 30, has reached his peak transfer value, leaving for £22m, and the data suggests he will start to decline. In two years, Palace have made a £16m profit and replaced him with Anan Khalaili, whom they believe is a younger version with a higher ceiling. On his debut against Manchester City, the similarities were striking, with the Israeli wing-back relentless from start to finish. Those two transfers were net zero, too.

Quinten Timber, an athletic ball-winner, adds a desperately required profile to Palace’s midfield options, replacing bit-part player Devenny, who moved to Stoke City on a permanent deal.

Losing Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest was emotionally tough for Palace. But, from a business perspective, it was the right move

Quinten Timber, an athletic ball-winner, adds a desperately required profile to Palace’s midfield

Adam Wharton and Kamada is a strong pairing but against superior opposition, the two-man midfield has lacked athleticism and bite at times. Timber gives Sage a plan B.

Some sources have suggested Timber’s physical profile should suit the Premier League, given his brother Jurrien’s success at Arsenal. His arrival also helps solve the problem of losing Kamada to the Asia Cup in the new year.

Ben Chilwell – if he can stay fit – is an upgrade on Borna Sosa, who failed to make an impact last season. Chilwell, signed for free from Strasbourg, was at the club on loan from Chelsea when Palace won the FA Cup. He is a leader, homegrown and offensively talented.

His injury record is alarming but he did manage 34 games at Strasbourg last season. Sosa, who has joined Cologne on loan, played a third of the minutes Chilwell did last season because he was not at the level required.

What Palace have successfully done this window is build a complete squad, with multiple options in every position. That was the bugbear last season.

They have a 28-man group, six of whom will need to be cut from the European squad, giving Sage the ability to rotate with at least two players for every position.

Of course, the window could have been improved if moves for Joel Ordonez and Malick Fofana had gone through. But Ordonez’s medical showed his broken metatarsal injury was more serious than initially expected, meaning he would not have been an option until later in the season.

It could be a deal Palace revisit in January. The highly-rated centre back should be available by then and has long been admired by the club.

Ben Chilwell (left) signed for free from Strasbourg and was at Palace on loan from Chelsea when they won the FA Cup

Fofana’s move from Lyon was ultimately hijacked by Sunderland after Palace thought they had beaten the North East club to his signature. Palace sources were frustrated on Tuesday afternoon, as Sunderland offered the player’s family money they could not match. Sage desperately wanted to sign him after working together at Lyon.

There has been significant player turnover at Palace and it will take time for the squad to gel – 11 players have arrived with six first-teamers making way.

On the whole, they are in a stronger position than last year, with a proficient starting XI and solid back-up in every position. That gives them plenty of reason to be optimistic. The proof will be on the pitch but the signs are promising.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fears Andoni Iraola must have an awkward conversation with £350,000-a-week Dominik Szoboszlai - after 'massive transfer mistake' created a 'mess' at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai and move him to right-back permanently.

Szoboszlai, 25, was rewarded with a new £350,000-a-week contract this summer after being named Liverpool’s Player of the Season for his impressive performances in midfield last campaign - one of the few positives in what was otherwise a disappointing season for the Reds under Arne Slot.

Despite establishing himself as a mainstay in midfield, the Hungarian has also been called upon to deputise at right-back, doing so sporadically last season and again during the second half of Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Carragher believes Szoboszlai may be tasked with the right-back role permanently after Liverpool's disjointed start under Iraola, who has drawn both his Premier League matches so far.

With Conor Bradley still injured and Jeremie Frimpong struggling for form, right-back has become a problem position for Liverpool since Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit to Real Madrid last summer.

Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai (left) and move him to right-back

Carragher fears Liverpool made a 'massive mistake' by not recruiting at full-back this summer

Fearing it was a 'massive mistake' not to bolster Liverpool's ranks at full-back in the transfer window, Carragher is confident Szoboszlai could provide a solution for Iraola.

'The big thing he (Iraola) has got, and it happened last season and at the weekend, Szoboszlai went back to right-back. I've never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player,' Carragher said on the Stick to Football podcast, brought to you by Disney+.

'Now, he's signed a new contract and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he's almost said "I want to play midfield". He's moved around a bit and he started the season in central midfield. I don't see him as that.

'For me, in midfield he's a Jordan Henderson. Runner, energy, with more of a goal threat. But Liverpool don't play that way and he's not really a No 10. His best role could actually be at right-back. He'd get plenty of the ball, he can run and almost play that Trent role from there.

'But there's no way he's going to want to play there because he's just signed a new contract for £350,000 a week. You've just done this big thing, he's the vice-captain, I just think that's a conversation Iraola is going to have to have going forward, because the midfield is not right and he's part of that midfield not being right.'

Liverpool reinforced Iraola's ranks this summer with the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and the £34.5m acquisition of Victor Munoz from Osasuna, who both play on the left wing.

Centre-backs Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo also signed on permanent and loan deals respectively to bolster the defence, but no additions were made at full-back or in central midfield.

'I'm stunned,' Gary Neville said reflecting on Liverpool's transfer window.

'The two full-backs (Kerkez and Frimpong), it was quite clear at the start of last season when you watched them for five or six matches that defensively they weren't going to be quite at the level to do it. I'm stunned, will Liverpool regret not bringing players in there?'

Szoboszlai won Liverpool's Player of the Season last term for his performances in midfield

He took over from Jeremie Frimpong at right-back against Nottingham Forest last weekend

Carragher added: 'Their understanding of the game is really really poor. You're watching the game and thinking why he's done that? I described Kerkez at the start of last season as the "Darwin Nunez" of full-backs. It's just head down and run. Everything Kerkez does is 100 miles per hour.

'They brought in Kerkez for £40million, he's had a first season. Wasn't amazing, but it's probably right to give him another go. Iraola's come in from Bournemouth, he knows him, okay. You're our left back for the season.

'The right-back situation is a mess. What Liverpool did when Trent left, and I agreed with it, they didn't go and buy a Trent replacement. Conor Bradley has done well enough when he's fit and they brought Frimpong in, not as direct competition, but almost for a bit of right-back and a bit of right-wing, to get his minutes there.

'Bradley got his chance, got an injury and didn't do particularly well last season, let's be honest. My problem with it is, Conor Bradley is a good young player, but if someone gets a bad injury, he's not that good that you don't go and replace him.

'You'd wait for Trent and Andy Robertson to come back, but unfortunately I don't think you should be waiting for Conor Bradley. You go and buy a right-back.

'We're Liverpool, we're a big club, we can't wait for Conor Bradley. We want to get him back and good luck to him, but I think it's a massive mistake.'

Liverpool will be searching for their first win of the season when they head to Portman Road to face newly promoted Ipswich on Friday.

Sports.title: From 'Big Moves Hughes' to Public Enemy No 1 - how Liverpool's Saudi-bound transfer chief Richard Hughes left Reds brutally undercooked
Sports.content:
From 'Big Moves Hughes' to Public Enemy No 1 - how Liverpool's Saudi-bound transfer chief Richard Hughes left Reds brutally undercooked

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Like Arne Slot, history might be kind to Liverpool’s sporting director Richard Hughes – but right now, fans will be in no rush to wave off his farewell plane.

He was the man that recruited Slot himself, after all. When Jurgen Klopp quit, Hughes thought out of the box and identified a replacement that, really, no fan was calling for. Twelve months later, Slot and Hughes were on the Anfield pitch holding aloft the Premier League trophy.

Hughes was also the man who convinced Florian Wirtz to join the club when pretty much every team in Europe fancied him.

A few weeks later, Hughes and Slot handled themselves with class in public statements and private actions when Diogo Jota tragically died in a car crash at just 28.

The Scottish transfer chief was the man who recruited Alexander Isak when the word from Newcastle all summer was that the Swede simply was not for sale.

Neither Isak or Wirtz have flourished just yet but both are showing signs that this could be their year – and that their axis could be frightening for opponents up and down the land.

Richard Hughes was the man who appointed Arne Slot, and together the pair were celebrating the Premier League title a year later. Now the picture looks very different, however

Hughes' big-money purchases of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz are yet to bear fruit

At the end of that record-breaking transfer window in 2025, where Liverpool spent a whopping £446million, Hughes was adored by supporters and made into internet memes. ‘Big Moves Hughes’, one member of the YouTube channel Redmen TV dubbed him.

The poor chap who came up with that nickname is reminded of it every day because a year on, ‘Big Moves Hughes’ is now heading for his own big move – to Saudi Arabia – and few fans will be sad to see him go.

There is a small section of Liverpool fans on social media that seem to spend the majority of their waking hours shouting at screens or sending abusive messages to people they have never met in person.

It says something, then, that Hughes has been public enemy No 1 at times this summer.

This ire comes in a window where they have a bigger net spend than anyone in the league, with one buy just £2million shy of the British transfer record.

Since winning the Premier League title, in fact, Liverpool have spent £693million on first-team players.

So why does everyone dislike Hughes?

The first reason is a stubbornness to strengthen certain positions on the pitch which leave new head coach Andoni Iraola, who Hughes has now recruited at both Bournemouth and Liverpool, brutally undercooked.

Signing Bradley Barcola is a fine bit of business and a potential game-changer – but can the Reds achieve their dreams this season when they are so blatantly light at full back and central midfield?

Signing Bradley Barcola is a fine bit of business and a potential game-changer – but can the Reds achieve their dreams this season when they are so blatantly light in other positions?

Jeremie Frimpong, who has struggled for form this season, is the only fit right back at the club

As they have shown in both games so far, scoring goals will be no issue whatsoever. It is the fact 35-year-old Virgil van Dijk and his new defensive partner Jeremy Jacquet resemble soldiers entering a battlefield with no armour.

You could have the best artillery and weapons in the world but you will not win the war if your troops cannot defend their position, too.

The need for a deeper-lying midfield is not a new thing, nor is it an overreaction to two league fixtures. They have been crying out for one since Fabinho left in 2023, arguably even further when you note the Brazilian started to decline before his exit.

At full back, Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez might come good eventually. For now, though, they are both seismic downgrades on Trent Alexander-Arnold and a prime Andy Robertson.

Frimpong is the only fit right back at the club, with Conor Bradley missing since January with a horrific knee injury. If the Dutchman, noticeably poor in the opening fixtures, gets injured – as he did a lot last term – there is no back-up.

They could ask loanee Ronald Araujo to cover, but he is needed also to cover at centre back where Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni are both on the treatment table. At left back, Kerkez’s deputy is Kostas Tsimikas, who struggled for minutes on loan at Roma last term.

There is a need to be realistic and we know there is no money tree at Anfield. But not signing a midfielder again – and another full back – leaves Liverpool incredibly short. If this turns out to be an unsuccessful season, fan ire may not turn to new boss Iraola but the board.

Given the money spent, it is categorically wrong to accuse anyone of lacking ambition, as some supporters have done. But it is fair to question the plan and ask whether the posh seats give a different view on the game. From where everyone else sits, midfield is a glaring weakness.

As Hughes heads for the exit door, it is hard to escape the feeling that new boss Andoni Iraola has been left short-changed

Instead, most of Hughes’s eggs were in the forward basket. Yankuba Minteh and Ismaila Sarr were targeted but ultimately came to nothing. In fairness, neither made sense: Sarr is 28 and not an upgrade on potential departee Cody Gakpo; Minteh has potential but is injured right now.

Liverpool had known of Mohamed Salah’s exit for half a year yet it felt like they were panicking in the last 10 days of the window.

Leaders Van Dijk and Alisson are both only contracted until the end of this season. Gomez, Tsimikas and Wataru Endo are also in the same boat.

So next summer is already shaping up to be busy as Liverpool feels like a carousel of chaos in a revolving state of transition. It is likely that Hughes will have his feet up in Saudi Arabia, with a move to Al Hilal having been in the works for months.

The sporting director might be remembered more fondly once the likes of Isak and Wirtz click, plus the two wingers he signed this summer – Barcola and Victor Munoz – look like shrewd business.

But as this summer window closes and Hughes heads for the exit door, it is hard to escape the feeling that Iraola has been left short-changed and that, for all the glamorous assets Liverpool have, there are still several design faults not fixed.

Sports.title: Aryna Sabalenka unleashes on 'joke' reporter in press conference tirade about her US Open 'partying'
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka lashed out at an award-winning New York Times sportswriter on Wednesday over a question following her US Open victory.

Following a dominant 6-1, 6-1 second-round victory over Polina Iatcenko, Sabalenka was asked by Matthew Futterman about her recent sponsorship obligations heading into the tournament.

The tennis star has been seen at many events for brands she works with, including for Gucci and luxury jewellery store Material Good, leading up to her singles campaign at the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York.

'How are you finding your mood now that the tournament has started?' asked Futterman, who now works for New York Times-owned website The Athletic. 'Obviously last week it's lots of parties and fun and stuff like that.'

The two-time reigning US Open champion was in no mood. 'You guys are like a joke,' she said. 'Parties? Fun? Why would you even say that?

'Why would you even think about that? Like, what kind of question is that? Just because I posted some activities with brands and you think that I've been partying?'

Futterman quickly tried to explain that he wasn't suggesting she was partying, saying 'I'm saying there are a lot of events and things like that,' but Sabalenka disagreed.

Aryna Sabalenka was not happy with a question she received during her U.S. Open press conference, ‘Think before you say stuff’



“How are you finding your mood now that the tournament has started? Obviously last week it’s lots of parties and fun and stuff like that..”



Aryna: “You… pic.twitter.com/CPZvShRbSI — The Tennis Letter (@TheTennisLetter) September 3, 2026

Aryna Sabalenka snapped back at journalist Matthew Futterman's question after her US Open win on Wednesday

Sabalenka had attended a number of events following her arrival in New York for the tournament

Futterman, seen here in 2016, said he did not mean to suggest Sabalenka was unfocused

'You literally said that,' she said. Futterman then pleaded his case to fellow reporters: 'For everyone who's unclear, I'm not suggesting that Aryna is having fun at these parties. I'm saying she makes a lot of appearances and there's a lot to do.'

Again, Sabalenka was unimpressed and simply responded by saying 'OK'.

Still not defeated, Futterman made one final attempt to ask Sabalenka about her transition from celebrity endorser back into athlete-mode.

'Now that the tournaments started, do you find you're getting quite serious and combative?' he asked.

'Oh yeah, I wasn't serious before that,' she said. 'Next question.' And just in case she hadn't made herself clear, Sabalenka added one last dig: 'Think before you say stuff.'

The Daily Mail has sought further comment from Futterman.

Next up for Sabalenka is Kamilla Rakhimova in the third round on Friday in Queens.

Wednesday's exchange followed what had been a successful day for Sabalenka, who has faced criticism from trolls over her choice of Nike-designed outfits in the tournament.

She wore a black laced outfit as she walked around the city with fiance Georgios Frangulis

The 28-year-old is into fashion and often dons eye-catching outfits on and off the court

The world No1 turned heads after wearing a black basketball-inspired ensemble that left her electric orange sports bra and matching briefs completely exposed during the mixed doubles.

The two-time reigning singles champion then donned a similar outfit in Queens on Monday, only this time completely in bright orange, when she beat Camila Osorio 6-4, 6-4 to begin her run.

But for her second round match on Arthur Ashe on Wednesday, Sabalenka returned to the court in a black ensemble. However, this time, her sports bra and matching briefs were also black.

After Monday night's eye-catching orange look, Sabalenka explained the change was because sponsor Nike actually developed day and night versions of the outfit for her to wear during the tournament.

'To be honest, I didn't know that I have a day dress,' she said. 'I thought I have a black dress with orange underneath. I figured [out] when I went to Nike that I actually have day session and night session, which is just like black and orange for the day.'

Tennis fans were quick to slam the risque outfit that Sabalenka wore during the mixed doubles event with Djokovic, although she did not back down from criticism.

'Who cares what people think?' she told reporters at Flushing Meadows on Friday's media day, adding: 'I love it.'

Sports.title: Fenerbahce issue Mason Greenwood statement as UEFA investigate ex-Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Fenerbahce issue Mason Greenwood statement as UEFA investigate ex-Man Utd star

Mason Greenwood is under investigation following the chaotic and ugly scenes that followed Fenerbahce's Champions League victory over Lyon last month

View 2 Images Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi are being investigated by UEFA (Image: (OLIVIER CHASSIGNOLE / AFP via Getty Images))

Fenerbahce have confirmed that UEFA are investigating Mason Greenwood for his role in the chaotic and ugly scenes that followed his side’s Champions League qualifying play-off against Lyon. The encounter in France, which Greenwood’s side won 2-1, was marred by ugly scenes following the full-time final whistle.

‌



Greenwood’s team-mate, Matteo Guendouzi, who played for Lyon's arch-rivals Marseille between 2021 and 2024, provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch after his side’s victory at Groupama Stadium.

‌



Clashes then broke out on the pitch and in the tunnel as players and staff from both sides got involved. A figure in what appears to be a Lyon tracksuit then emerged from the tunnel and seemed to try to aim a flying kick at Guendouzi.

‌



Former Manchester United man Greenwood was also caught up in the ugly scenes, and Fenerbahce have now confirmed that the pair are under investigation from UEFA.

A statement from the Super Lig club confirmed: "Following the UEFA Champions League Play-Off Round second leg match, UEFA has initiated disciplinary proceedings against our players Mattéo Guendouzi and Mason Greenwood, as well as against our club.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Our club will present the necessary defenses before the relevant UEFA bodies in order to protect the rights and interests of our players and Fenerbahçe during this process.

"The necessary information, documents, and defenses regarding the process will be submitted to UEFA, and developments are being closely monitored by our Club. We inform the public accordingly."

Speaking after the game, Guendouzi claimed he had been 'disrespected' by home supporters. He said: "You know, when you've got 60,000 people insulting your family, your mum, your children, even before the match - and nobody from the refereeing team tells the stadium to be quiet.

‌



"Because I know that in France, when this sort of thing happens, there comes a point where they'll speak to the supporters and the match might be stopped. For 90 minutes - even longer if you count the warm-up - they were insulting my family.

View 2 Images Players from Lyon and Fenerbahce clashed at the Groupama Stadium (Image: (Olivier CHASSIGNOLE / AFP via Getty Images))

“That really gets to you. If you want to banter, then it goes both ways. They insulted my mum and my family; to me, that was disrespectful."

‌



Ismail Kartal, the Fenerbahce head coach, also spoke about the scenes and said: “As a team we all stood together to support Guendouzi. Support was provided. That is what teamwork is all about.”

Greenwood joined Fenerbahce from Marseille on a four-year deal back in July. The 24-year-old has made the switch to Turkey for a fee of £33.25m, which will be paid in three instalments over three years.

Greenwood scored 48 times in 81 appearances for OM, having made the switch from Manchester United in July 2024, and was the second-highest scorer in Ligue 1 last term behind Rennes’ Esteban Lepaul. After booking their place in the group stage of this season’s Champions League, Fenerbahce will host Liverpool and face Atletico Madrid away, as well taking on Aston Villa (away), Roma (home), Shakhtar Donetsk (away), Villarreal (home), Slavia Prague (home) and LASK (away).

Sports.title: Chelsea plot move for another ex-Liverpool star despite transfer window closing
Sports.content:
Chelsea plot move for another ex-Liverpool star despite transfer window closing

Chelsea saw Enzo Fernandez leave on deadline day without landing a replacement and Xabi Alonso is now eyeing the free agent market to fill the void

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has left Chelsea to join Man City (Image: Manchester City FC)

Chelsea are weighing up a shock move for Georginio Wijnaldum after seeing Enzo Fernandez leave on deadline day and their move for a replacement fall through.

‌



The Blues were heavily involved in the major headlines on the last day of the transfer window, seeing Fernandez leave for Manchester City in a record £125million deal whilst their pursuit of Lamine Camara at Monaco failed to materialise.

‌



It has left Xabi Alonso light in midfield and, with the window closed, the west Londoners have turned to the free agent market. That has led them to Liverpool's former midfielder Wijnaldum, who left the club in 2021.

‌



Foot Mercato reports that Chelsea have contacted Wijnaldum, now 35, as they prepared to offer him a route back into the Premier League, where he previously played for the Reds and Newcastle.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Dutchman is on the market having left Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq in the summer and Alonso sees him as a good option in the interim given the experience he has in England's top flight - winning the title back in 2020 at Anfield.

‌



Wijnaldum made 277 appearances across his time in England, coming up with crucial goals and proving to be part of a hugely effective Liverpool midfield. He showed he can be still effective and scored 17 times in 34 outings for Al-Ettifaq last season, but didn't earn himself a new deal.

So far this season, with Alonso implementing his own philosophy, Romeo Lavia has started both games in the middle of the pitch. He's been partnered by Reece James and Cole Palmer whilst Fernandez was omitted from the team amid the talk of him moving away.

View 2 Images Georginio Wijnaldum won the Champions League and the Premier League whilst at Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Despite letting the World Cup winner leave Alonso maintained, when quizzed on the situation, that he was prepared to do what was best for the team.

Speaking after their 4-3 win over Brighton the new Chelsea boss said: "We will see. We want the best for team. If anything that will happen or develop, we are not sure. We are preparing for all the scenarios, but I know that from Wednesday, we have a team to challenge and I want to win."

The Blues also have Moises Caicedo, who signed in a £115m deal, as one of their key midfielders but the Ecuadorian limped off on Sunday.

Sports.title: Every Premier League club's squad value after huge summer of spending with Liverpool above Man Utd
Sports.content:
Every Premier League club's squad value after huge summer of spending with Liverpool above Man Utd

Premier League squads look a lot different after a record-breaking transfer window and their squad valuations have changed dramatically

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez's £125m move to Manchester City was the biggest deal of the transfer window (Image: Maja Hitij - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Manchester City boast the most valuable squad in the Premier League now that the summer transfer window is over. The late signing of Enzo Fernandez has pushed Enzo Maresca's side back to the perch of England's finest with a total squad value of around £1.24billion, according to Transfermarkt.

‌



However, there is no guarantee that expenditure equals results on the pitch. Just ask Tottenham after their record-breaking influx of players which has failed to bear fruit so far this season.

‌



City pulled off the £125million signing of Fernandez from Chelsea on deadline day to match the Premier League's record purchase. City also saw a lot of talent leave the Etihad Stadium but such as their strength in depth, they retain the highest squad value.

‌

‌



Chelsea would have remained inside the £1bn club had they held onto Fernandez. And despite spending big themselves with additions like £117m man Morgan Rogers, they're down to third with a valuation of £930m.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Man Utd deal announced, Arsenal double move, Folarin Balogun bombshell
Sports.content:
Latest transfer news from Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and more - as Premier League clubs break summer window record with £3.2billion spend

After a major summer of spending, the Premier League's summer transfer window drew to a close at 11pm on Tuesday evening. It was a record-shattering couple of months across the UK, with a total exceeding £3.2billion exceeded through deals.

Manchester City and Chelsea agreed a £125m deal for Enzo Fernandez, with the wantaway midfielder finally leaving Stamford Bridge after months of speculation regarding his future. The Cityzens also welcomed Iliman Ndiaye to their ranks in a £65m move, further bolstering Enzo Maresca's choice.

Sunderland's approach of Malick Fofana also dominated the headlines on Tuesday, with what should have been a straightforward move turning into quite the saga when Crystal Palace threatened to hijack the Black Cats' move.

With Kyril Louis-Dreyfus flying to Lyon to persuade the 21-year-old winger to join his project at the Stadium of Light, Fofana gave Sunderland the green-light to put the wheels in motion on a move, forced to submit a dealsheet to ensure a transfer due to the last-minute nature of his decision.

In West London, AS Monaco also knocked back Chelsea's £47m move for Lamine Camara in dramatic fashion. Everything had been agreed between the two clubs, when Monaco pulled the plug with just minutes to go until the deadline - with Everton's endeavours of securing Folarin Balogun having a knock-on effect.

Chelsea were reportedly left fuming with the incredibly unprofessional last-minute decision. And Balogun's deal didn't go through anyway, with Monaco's sporting director sensationally claiming it was the striker who walked away from the deal after 'feeling mistreated' during his medical.

Mykhailo Mudryk also joined Tottenham Hotspur on a season-long loan, with both clubs hopeful that the Ukrainian is able to reacclimate to the pace of the Premier League after a two-year lay-off.

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott says Liverpool teammate helped influence his Valencia loan move
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott says Liverpool teammate helped influence his Valencia loan move

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott completed a loan move to Spanish side Valencia this summer after spending last term with Aston Villa and one of his teammates played a big role in the switch

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott is set to spend the season on loan with Valencia (Image: Getty Images)

Harvey Elliott has revealed that Liverpool teammate Giorgi Mamardashvili convinced him to make a move to Valencia. The English midfielder completed a switch to the Spanish side late in the summer window, having fallen down the pecking order under Andoni Iraola.

‌



He is set to spend the season on-loan at the Mestalla, with no option to make the deal a permanent one.

‌



Explaining why he chose to pursue the switch, Elliott has confirmed he had conversations with goalkeeper Mamardashvili, who played 134 times for the La Liga side ahead of joining Liverpool.

‌



Speaking at his unveiling, Elliott said: “Giorgi told me the fans are incredible. When things aren’t going well, they support you and are with you until the end. And when you win and play well, they’re the best fans you could have.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“He also told me the city is amazing. We talked a little, although I didn’t want to ask too many questions so as not to give away what was going on. But Giorgi spoke very highly of the city and, above all, of the club. I’m very excited and eager to experience it for myself.”

‌



Meanwhile, he also confirmed that Valencia boss Carlos Corberan also had a considerable role to play. Elliott added: “It was my decision to come here.

"I had a few calls with Carlos Corberan, in which we talked about my objectives and what he expected of me as a player. The start of the season has been tricky, but there’s still a long way to go.”

Elliott’s move to Spain comes after a tricky few seasons in the Premier League. He spent last season on loan at Aston Villa but made just nine appearances and scored just one goal, with Villa opting not to sign him permanently.

‌



View 2 Images Giorgi Mamardashvili gave Elliott advice on a move to Valencia (Image: Getty Images)

And Elliott is now keen to rediscover his best form with his adoptive side. He said: “On a personal level, my goal is to regain my self-confidence, play freely and enjoy my football. I’m very grateful for the opportunity Valencia CF have given me. As a team, the goal is to achieve everything possible, and I want to contribute -starting this Sunday.”

Elliott joined Liverpool on a free transfer from Fulham back in 2019 and he has gone on to make 149 appearances for the Reds, scoring 15 goals. His current deal at Anfield is set to run until 2028.

Article continues below

Valencia will certainly hope that he can have an instant impact following their disappointing start to the season. They have just one point from their opening three games of the season ahead of this weekend’s clash with Barcelona.

Sports.title: Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool considered 8 wingers in summer transfer window before landing Bradley Barcola

Liverpool made Bradley Barcola their final signing of the summer after sealing a £123million deal with Paris Saint-Germain but the Reds had a number of alternatives to the French winger

View 2 Images Liverpool eventually sealed a deal for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool had as many as eight alternatives to Bradley Barcola in the summer transfer window, including England’s Anthony Gordon and Real Madrid star Endrick.

‌



The Reds came into the window needing additions out wide following Mohamed Salah’s exit. They eventually signed Barcola in a £123million deal after a summer-long search followed by drawn-out negotiations with former side Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



But it is well known that the Frenchman was not the only player that Liverpool chiefs had in mind. Former RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande was a high-profile target, albeit Real Madrid swooped in to seal his services instead.

‌



And that appears to have been the theme with a host of their potential attacking targets. Former Everton and Newcastle man Anthony Gordon was an early possibility but he instead moved to Barcelona for £69m after the Spanish side chose not to activate their permanent £26m option for Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Liverpool were also left frustrated as their attempts to sign Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh ended without a positive result. Brighton received bids of £50m and £60m for the Gambian but chose to turn them down.

While Minteh eventually stayed where he was, the same cannot be said of the rest of Liverpool’s shortlist. Matias Fernandez-Pardo had emerged as an option following his standout performances for French side Lille, with Newcastle sealing a late deal worth £51m for his services.

Lyon wideman Malick Fofana was also eyed by Liverpool, but he too opted for a move to the north east, having sealed a deadline day switch to Sunderland.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool were previously interested in Anthony Gordon (Image: Getty Images)

Away from Barcola, Liverpool also had another PSG winger in mind in their search for attacking reinforcements. Ibrahim Mbaye was eventually on the move to the Premier League but signed for Aston Villa.

Their final two options were Real Madrid’s Endrick and Koln’s Said El Mala, but they eventually stayed with their current clubs.

‌



That left Liverpool pursuing a deal for Barcola, who is keen to lift silverware at Anfield. He said: "I hope to achieve very big thingsFirst of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.

"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.

"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy. It took a long time but I'm really happy to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play."

Sports.title: Scott McTominay breaks silence on his upcoming heart surgery after Napoli statement
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay breaks silence on his upcoming heart surgery after Napoli statement

Scott McTominay has offered some clarity after Napoli announced that the Scotland international will undergo heart surgery on "a mild benign arrhythmia" in the coming days

View 2 Images Scott McTominay has explained his surgery (Image: Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

Scott McTominay has reassured Napoli and Scotland fans that he is "fine" after Napoli announced he would undergo heart surgery.

‌



The Italian club released a statement on Tuesday explaining the situation. It read: "Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days. He will be available again after the international break."

‌



While the announcement about his arrhythmia - an irregular heartbeat - came as a shock to many supporters, McTominay says it is nothing serious. “I’m fine, the procedure was something I’d planned to do with the club for quite a while,” he told reporters at the Gran Gala Del Calcio, the Italian equivalent of the PFA Awards, on Wednesday night.

‌



“We’d already talked about it in pre-season. I’ll be out for a few weeks.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

McTominay is a key player for Napoli, having joined the club from Manchester United for £25million in 2024. He has scored 27 goals in 82 games for Napoli and helped them win Serie A in 2024/25.

‌



He was named Serie A player of the year for 2025 for his incredible debut campaign and will be important to their efforts to reclaim the trophy following Inter Milan's triumph last season.

The 29-year-old midfielder has started both of Napoli's matches this season but is now set for a short spell on the sidelines. While he still has two years left on his contract, there has been some speculation in Italy over his future.

View 2 Images Scott McTominay is set for a spell on the sidelines (Image: Insidefoto, Insidefoto/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



“There haven’t been any new talks,” McTominay said when asked about a possible extension. “The important thing is what happens on the pitch, not the contract extension. I don’t know when it will happen, it’s not the time to be thinking about that.”

Napoli began the campaign with a 2-0 win over Genoa before losing 2-1 to Cesc Fabregas' Como on the weekend. Fellow former Manchester United player Rasmus Hojlund netted the consolation against Como, while ex-Manchester City star Kevin De Bruyne scored on the opening weekend.

Max Allegri is now the man in charge at Napoli and he explained after the Como defeat that McTominay was also dealing with a different kind of health issue.

‌



“McTominay had some problems with blisters, so he’s been training on a limited basis," Allegri said. "Hopefully, we can get him into the best possible condition as soon as possible.”

The Scottish star will sit out of the next four Napoli games and will be a big miss. Napoli take on Inter Milan on Saturday, ahead of a Champions League clash with Premier League champions Arsenal and further league games against Bologna and Fiorentina.

Sports.title: Richarlison agrees Tottenham exit with eye-watering deal to triple his salary
Sports.content:
Richarlison agrees Tottenham exit with eye-watering deal to triple his salary

Richarlison is one of the names to be mentioned throughout the summer transfer window.

View 2 Images Richarlison has been heavily linked with a move away from Tottenham. (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison has reportedly reached an agreement on personal terms with Turkish side Trabzonspor. The 29-year-old has been linked with a move away from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium throughout the summer transfer window.

‌



Richarlison was heavily linked with a return to former club Everton. The two clubs were in negotiations over a potential move for Iliman N'Diaye, who eventually completed a deadline day move to Manchester City.

‌



Amid the speculation, Richarlison appeared to hit out at Spurs in a statement released on Instagram. Despite the English transfer window being closed, it seems that the striker has made a decision over his future.

‌

With the Turkish transfer window remaining open until midnight on September 4, Transfermarkt reports that Richarlison could complete a switch to Trabzonspor, where he would link up with former Liverpool star Mohamed Salah in a mouth-watering attacking partnership.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:

Semi-final: Ukraine vs Sweden

Semi-final: Poland vs Albania
