World.title: 'Shared commitment to eradicate terrorism': PM Modi as India, Belgium sign key MoUs
World.content:
Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever, Prime Minister NArendra Modi

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India and Belgium on Thursday signed a series of MoUs and agreements aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation across renewable energy, defence, trade, investment, maritime affairs, critical minerals, semiconductors and research, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever held talks in New Delhi.The agreements were exchanged in the presence of PM Modi and De Wever at Hyderabad House, with the two sides seeking to turn the longstanding India-Belgium relationship into a broader strategic and economic partnership.PM Modi said the two countries had agreed to strengthen cooperation in several emerging areas, including startups, maritime capacity building, universities and research, while also working towards a Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement to facilitate the movement of talent."Today, we agreed to strengthen connections between our startups and enhance capacity building in the maritime sector. We will also reinforce cooperation in the university and research sectors, and we will soon sign a Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement to facilitate the movement of talent. Today we also held detailed discussions on regional and global developments. Both India and Belgium believe in the rule of law, dialogue, and diplomacy..."The Prime Minister also highlighted the renewable energy MoU signed during the visit, saying it would provide fresh momentum to bilateral cooperation on sustainability. The two countries have additionally decided to enhance cooperation in the processing and recycling of critical minerals."Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we have agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries. Agreements reached between our governments and defence industries will open up new opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation against crime between our respective agencies. A clean energy future and reliable supply chains are our shared priorities. The MoU on renewable energy signed today will give new momentum to our cooperation on sustainability. We have decided to enhance cooperation in the processing and recycling of critical minerals. Belgium's expertise in semiconductors and India's scale complement each other; in this regard, we will work together to integrate Belgium's IMEC Institute with India's semiconductor ecosystem. People-to-people ties are the greatest strength of our relationship."The two sides also discussed ways to strengthen economic ties following the conclusion of the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement earlier this year. PM Modi said India and Belgium had taken several steps to translate the opportunities created by the agreement into concrete economic outcomes."Earlier this year, we concluded a historic Free Trade Agreement between India and the European Union. This unprecedented cooperation between two of the world's largest democratic powers will further strengthen global stability, growth, and shared prosperity. India's sustained economic progress and this agreement have opened up new possibilities for our economic ties. Today, we have taken several significant steps to translate these possibilities into concrete results. We have established an 'Investment Fast-Track Mechanism' in India for Belgian companies. We have decided to make the India-Belgium Business Forum a regular mechanism. We will enhance synergy between the financial, fintech, and regulatory institutions of both nations, and through these measures, we will realize the goal of doubling bilateral trade over the next five years"Defence cooperation emerged as another key component of the agreements and discussions. PM Modi said India and Belgium had agreed to increase military exchanges and training, while government and defence industry agreements would create opportunities for co-development and co-production of defence equipment.He also said the two countries would strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between their agencies to combat crime.PM Modi said India and Belgium were also working together on modern defence equipment and cited the Zorawar tank as an example of the expanding partnership."I had the opportunity to visit Belgium ten years ago, and I am delighted to see the remarkable progress our partnership has made over the past decade. Today, the scope of our cooperation has expanded beyond traditional sectors to encompass strategic areas such as defense and clean energy. We are collaborating on modern defence equipment, such as the Zorawar tank. We are also developing one of the world's largest green ammonia projects in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh. "On clean energy and technology, PM Modi said the renewable energy agreement would strengthen cooperation on sustainability, while the proposed integration of Belgium's IMEC Institute with India's semiconductor ecosystem would combine Belgian expertise with India's scale.The two countries also discussed critical minerals, particularly their processing and recycling, as both sides look to build more reliable supply chains.PM Modi said the latest agreements marked an expansion of ties beyond traditional areas such as diamonds and trade."Last month, Belgium and the Netherlands jointly hosted the Hockey World Cup. I extend my heartiest congratulations to you for the magnificent organization of this World Cup. I also commend our players for their hard work and performance. Diamonds have long linked India and Belgium. Today, we are transforming this historic bond into a comprehensive partnership. I am confident that our discussions today mark the beginning of a new chapter in our bilateral relations. .."The Prime Minister also placed the bilateral engagement in the context of ongoing global conflicts and geopolitical uncertainty, saying India and Belgium supported efforts towards peace while sharing a commitment to combating terrorism."... Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts towards an early end to conflict and the establishment of peace; furthermore, eradicating terrorism in all its forms is our shared commitment. Last month, Belgium and the Netherlands jointly hosted the Hockey World Cup. I extend my heartiest congratulations to you for the magnificent organization of this World Cup. I also commend our players for their hard work and performance. Diamonds have long linked India and Belgium. Today, we are transforming this historic bond into a comprehensive partnership. I am confident that our discussions today mark the beginning of a new chapter in our bilateral relations..."PM Modi said the broader global environment remained challenging, with conflicts affecting food and fuel security as well as supply chains. He said India's economy had continued to maintain its momentum despite the uncertainty."The world is currently going through a period of great upheaval. Conflict situations persist in various parts of the globe, and uncertainty is impacting sectors ranging from food and fuel to supply chains. Even amidst this challenging environment, the Indian economy has maintained its momentum; we recorded a growth rate of 7.8% in the last quarter. Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world. "The agreements and discussions came during De Wever's first visit to India as Belgian Prime Minister. He is in the country from September 2 to 4 at the invitation of PM Modi. His visit is also the first by a Belgian Prime Minister to India in two decades.De Wever, who took office in February 2025, is accompanied by Belgium's Minister of Defence and Foreign Trade, Theo Francken, along with a high-level delegation of officials and business leaders, including representatives from the Belgian defence industry.Earlier on Thursday, Francken held the India-Belgium Defence Ministers' Meeting with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, where both sides discussed expanding defence cooperation and greater engagement between their defence industries."The world is witnessing a time of great geopolitical and economic turmoil. Most of it is not our doing, but we have to handle the challenges. In such situations, meeting a friend and partner like you provides a useful opportunity to exchange views and perspectives," Singh said.Singh said the recently held India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue had provided a framework for taking the bilateral partnership forward, particularly in defence and security."We welcome greater cooperation with Belgian and Indian defence companies," he said.Francken, meanwhile, called for deeper cooperation with India, highlighting the country's technological capabilities and saying Belgium needed partners such as India for future projects."We can learn so much from you. You are a high-technology country. You are one of the most densely populated countries, and we really need to work together because Belgium is an old Western European country with a lot of technology, but we need countries like India. We need to collaborate on future projects, and for Belgium, this is the way forward"Francken also referred to Belgium's economic mission to India led by Princess Astrid in March 2025, describing it as a first step towards a renewed relationship between the two countries.He said the mission had helped generate momentum in bilateral ties, with contracts being signed on collaboration projects within 18 months."That is amazing. This means that we worked hard, that our people worked hard, and that we can go further in this pathway."The Belgian minister also said De Wever's visit had a packed agenda focused on expanding bilateral cooperation."I'm very happy to be here with our Prime Minister. For first time in more than 20 years a Belgian Prime Minister is visiting your beautiful country. We have a busy, busy schedule with lot of signing ceremonies, a lot of good talks with the Prime Ministerâ¦"Francken said Belgium and India could address the geopolitical challenges facing the world through greater friendship and partnership."I think it's totally right when you talk about geopolitical challenges that we have to meet. We didn't organise them, we didn't always want them, but we need to be realistic, and we need to go further. And we can do this in friendship and partnership between Belgium and India."The latest agreements build on growing economic engagement between the two countries. A Belgian Economic Mission led by Princess Astrid in March 2025 brought together 338 participants from companies, chambers of commerce, academia and public institutions and resulted in 38 MoUs.De Wever also paid tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat on Thursday, where he laid a wreath and offered flowers before signing the visitor's book.The Belgian Prime Minister's visit is aimed at further strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation across trade, investment, defence, technology and connectivity, while also giving fresh momentum to India's engagement with the European Union and Europe.

World.title: Manipur violence: 306 killed, 49 missing since May 2023
World.content:
At least 306 people have been killed and 49 remain missing in the ethnic violence that broke out in Manipur in May 2023, state home minister Govindas Konthoujam told the Assembly on Thursday.

Responding to a query by BJP MLA Sapam Ranjan Singh on the second day of the ongoing Assembly session, Konthoujam said the figures were recorded as of August 31, 2026.

âSince the violence started on May 3, 2023, 306 people have died, and 49 people are still missing as of August 31, 2026,â he said.

Violence erupted over ST status demand

The ethnic clashes between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities began on May 3, 2023, after a âTribal Solidarity Marchâ was organised in the hill districts to protest the Meitei communityâs demand for Scheduled Tribe status.

Meiteis account for around 53 per cent of Manipurâs population and live mainly in the Imphal Valley, while tribals, including Nagas and Kukis, constitute around 40 per cent and reside predominantly in the hill districts.

The prolonged violence resulted in widespread displacement and triggered significant political developments in the state.

Presidentâs Rule revoked earlier this year

Presidentâs Rule was imposed in Manipur on February 13, 2025, after then chief minister N Biren Singh resigned amid the prolonged ethnic conflict. The 60-member Assembly was subsequently placed under suspended animation.

Presidentâs Rule was revoked on February 4, 2026, paving the way for the formation of a new government under BJP leader Yumnam Khemchand Singh as chief minister.

World.title: Jagan, Sharmila pay tributes to YSR in Kadapa district on 17th death anniversary
World.content:
Former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy and Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee president Y.S. Sharmila paid tributes to their father, former Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy, at his grave at Idupulapaya in Kadapa district on Wednesday (September 2, 2026), the 17th anniversary of his death. The duo visited separately, as they have since their political parting.

Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy arrived at the YSR Estates with his wife Y.S. Bharathi Reddy and other family members, garlanded the Samadhi and sat in silence for a few minutes. He also garlanded the bust of his father on the premises. “Miss you always, dad...! You will forever be my inspiration,” he wrote on X. Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy, his maternal uncle and YSRCP Kadapa district president P. Ravindranath Reddy, and former Chandragiri MLA Chevireddy Bhaskar Reddy were among those present.

Miss you always, Dad! You'll forever be my inspiration. pic.twitter.com/4e9pkYxlem — YS Jagan Mohan Reddy (@ysjagan) September 2, 2026

Ms. Sharmila offered a garland and a wreath at the Samadhi. She called her father the “heartbeat” of the crores of Telugus who had benefited from Jalayagnam, fee reimbursement, free power for agriculture and Aarogyasri, and said the State would always remain indebted to him. “All the projects considered to be his pet schemes are hard to imagine and impossible for any other leader to implement. The schemes will always bear the imprint of YSR,” she said. She had prayed for the well-being and prosperity of the State, she said.

The man they remembered

Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy was Chief Minister of undivided Andhra Pradesh from 2004 until his death, a Lok Sabha member from Kadapa for four terms and an MLA from Pulivendula for six. He died on September 2, 2009, months after leading the Congress to a second consecutive victory, when the helicopter carrying him went missing over the Nallamala forest; the wreck was found the next day, and all five aboard were dead. Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy, then a Congress MP, left the party and founded the YSRCP; Ms. Sharmila, after a party of her own in Telangana, merged it with the Congress and took over its Andhra Pradesh unit in 2024.

World.title: Tamil Nadu government identifies three sites for the new Assembly-Secretariat complex
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government, which has identified three sites for the proposed Assembly-Secretariat complex in Chennai, is expected to make its final choice and announce it by the middle of this month.

The sites identified by the government are: the Highways Research Station (HRS) in Guindy; a residential colony established by the Tamil Nadu Housing Board in Pattinapakkam (Foreshore Estate); and the plot once occupied by the now-defunct Indian Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (IDPL) in Nandambakkam.

Merits, demerits of the three sites

Each site has its own pros and cons. For instance, the HRS complex, located opposite the Lok Bhavan, is accessible through a fairly broad Sardar Patel Road. In fact, this formed a part of the area chosen by the AIADMK regime under Jayalalithaa for the Secretariat complex in 2003. Later that year, she laid the foundation stone for the Secretariat project, which covered about 43 acres and extended from the Gandhi Mandapam Road-end to the HRS on Sardar Patel Road. The proximity of the HRS compound to Anna University, where a large number of students are studying, is a factor that needs to be kept in mind.

Though not located on roads as wide as those in the case of the HRS, the sites of Foreshore Estate and Nandambakkam are in accessible spots. It is a matter of time before Chennai Metro Rail services, covering Nandambakkam too, will be inaugurated, while Foreshore Estate is located closer to Adyar and Mylapore, two important areas of Chennai. However, Foreshore Estate is in a critical yet dreaded part of the city for commuters.

Two of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s predecessors, Jayalalithaa and M. Karunanidhi, had attempted to shift the Secretariat from the existing Fort St. George. While Jayalalithaa’s efforts were futile, Karunanidhi had constructed a new Secretariat building at the Omandurar Government Estate, but Jayalalithaa, upon returning to power in 2011, had converted it into a multi-speciality hospital.

World.title: Former Indian Air Force Group Captain Abhinandan Varthaman joins regional airline FLY91 as pilot
World.content:
Former Indian Air Force Group Captain and Vir Chakra awardee Abhinandan Varthaman has joined Goa-based regional airline FLY91 as a pilot, according to sources.

Mr. Varthaman, who downed an enemy jet during an aerial combat with Pakistan in 2019 and was held captive for three days in that country, was honoured with the Vir Chakra award in 2021.

The sources told PTI that Mr. Varthaman joined the airline as a pilot in August.

When contacted, a FLY91 spokesperson said personal information about employees is a private matter and did not comment.

Further details could not be immediately ascertained.

The fighter pilot of the Indian Air Force was decorated with Vir Chakra — India's third-highest wartime gallantry medal — for displaying an "exceptional sense of duty" during the dogfight, as per the award citation.

World.title: Delhi-bound AI Express flight makes precautionary landing at Lucknow airport after smoke alarm goes off
World.content:
An Air India Express flight from Varanasi to Delhi made a precautionary landing at Lucknow airport on Thursday morning (September 3, 2026) allegedly after a smoke detection alarm went off in the aircraft's cargo hold.

However, preliminary checks at Lucknow airport found no sign of smoke or fire in the aircraft, they added.

Flight IX 1253, with 155 passengers onboard, took off from Varanasi airport around 8 am. Shortly after take-off, the smoke detection alarm in the cargo hold was activated, following which the pilot contacted Lucknow Air Traffic Control (ATC) and sought permission to land.

The aircraft landed at Lucknow airport at 8.52 a.m., following which the airport's response team, fire brigade personnel and technical experts reached the aircraft. All 155 passengers and crew members were deboarded at 9.02 a.m., sources said.

An Air India Express spokesperson said the crew operating the Varanasi-Delhi flight, prioritising passenger safety, opted for a precautionary diversion to Lucknow after a technical issue was detected.

The aircraft landed safely and all passengers were provided refreshments upon arrival at Lucknow airport. An alternative aircraft is being arranged on priority to take the passengers to their destination, the airline added.

The aircraft was moved to a hanger, where preliminary inspection found no signs of smoke or fire inside the aircraft, sources said, adding that investigation is under way to determine the reason for the activation of the smoke alarm.

World.title: Gloria Steinem, a potent voice of U.S. feminism and co-founder of Ms. Magazine, has died
World.content:
Gloria Steinem, the celebrated author and activist who became one of the most visible symbols and potent voices of the U.S. women’s movement and a fierce advocate for feminist causes throughout her life, has died. She was 92.

With her trademark streaked hair parted down the middle and large aviator glasses, Steinem, a co-founder of Ms. Magazine, was a hugely recognisable presence wherever she went. And she went everywhere: Much of her life as an advocate was spent on the road, speaking at college campuses and community centers, at rallies and marches.

She died on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) at her home in New York City, according to her and her foundation’s social media pages.

“You can’t do it on the phone or on the web,” she told The Associated Press in a 2015 interview. “You have to be there with all five senses. It should be obvious that people can’t empathise with each other unless we’re in same room.”

She began her career as a journalist, notably one who reported, in 1963, on degrading conditions in Hugh Hefner’s Playboy empire, an undercover assignment she came to later regret. She credits a meeting six years later, where women spoke out boldly in favor of abortion rights, with changing her career path.

“That speak-out was the beginning of activism for me,” Steinem, who had undergone a secret illegal abortion herself at age 22, told The AP in an email in 2022, reflecting on the reversal of Roe v Wade. “Either our control over our own bodies is equal, regardless of sex or race, or we’re not living in a democracy.”

The second day of a two-day international conference, ‘Act For Nutrition: The Emergency We Can No Longer Ignore’, is being held at Islamabad’s Serena Hotel. The conference aims to address Pakistan’s persistent nutrition and stunting crisis.

On the first day, experts at the conference warned that more than four in 10 children under five were stunted and malnutrition was costing Pakistan close to $17 billion annually.

They also said that malnutrition was produced by a combination of poor diets, inadequate healthcare, weak water and sanitation services, poverty and other factors, making a multisectoral response essential.

The two-day conference is bringing together policymakers, international development leaders, health professionals and nutrition experts to confront the burgeoning crisis and build momentum for urgent, coordinated action.

View the full agenda here.

3:45pm - Addressing malnutrition collective responsibility: Sarwat Gillani

Actress Sarwat Gillani said that addressing malnutrition was a collective responsibility.

“It should be portrayed as everyone’s responsibility because only then can it be resolved because it is in every province,” Gillani said.

“So we have to work on this problem collectively,” she added.

3:40pm - Sarwat Gillani stresses use of ‘intelligent marketing’

Actress Sarwat Gilani emphasised the use of “intelligent marketing” in addressing societal issues, including malnutrition.

“Intelligent marketing is the answer to so many of our problems. In this day and age where everything is on a credit card or a mobile phone [..] if we have all the right creative minds along with experts, we can all sit down and come up with a strategic marketing campaign,” she said.

3:30pm - Film mogul highlights importance of radio, PTV in reaching the masses

Satish Anand, the chairman of EverReady Pictures, highlighted the importance of radio and PTV for reaching the masses.

He said that radio was widely listened to by people living in rural areas. He added that PTV could also be effectively used to communicate social issues.

Satish Anand, the chairman of EverReady Pictures speaks at the conference. — White Star/ Tanveer Shahzad

3:20pm - Sarwat Gilani says malnutrition caused by host of factors

Actress Sarwat Gilani, who is also an ambassador for Special Olympics Pakistan and the Indus Hospital and Health Network, said that there had been a lot of “repetition” during the conference as people cited data and statistics.

“If this repetition, can be disseminated on an every day level, it would have a more lasting result,” she said. She said that malnutrition was not a “disease” and was caused by a host of factors.

She also called for focusing on the solution rather than the problem.

Actress Sarwat Gillani speaks at the conference. — White Star/ Tanveer Shahzad

3:17pm - Journalist notes lack of focus on nutrition in media

Journalist Zarrar Khuhro termed malnutrition a “silent crisis” and went on to say that there was limited conversation about the issue in the media.

“You will see a press release perhaps [..] but that does not cause a conversation at the household level and [..] if you can’t do that, then you have no hope of societal change”.

“That is what we need, not just top-down change but critical mass at the family level, personal individual level, identifying this issue and seeking solutions and creating what we call a public buy-in,” he said.

Journalist Zarrar Khuhro speaks at the conference, — White Star/ Tanveer Shahzad

3:12pm - Panel discussion on communicating for change begins

A panel discussion on communicating for societal change has now begun.

3:10pm - Official says 1 in 4 children in Punjab suffering from stunted growth

Dr Usman Ali Khan, the programme director of the Punjab Family Planning Programme, said that comparing the surveys from 2018 and 2024 showed progress.

However, despite this improvement, there were 5.5m malnourished children in the province, he said. He said that one in four children in the province suffered from stunted growth.

He said that the province was actively screening women and children that could be suffering from malnutrition and stunting.

3:05pm - Nutritional financing a provincial budgetary question, says Punjab govt official

Punjab government’s special secretary, Aurangzaib Haider Khan, presented three priorities to the forum.

“First, a common nutritional indicator so that provincial data can be compared, rather than merely collected,” Khan said.

Secondly, he called for an “honest recognition of the fiscal architecture [under] the 18th Amendment” and added that nutritional financing was predominantly a provincial budgetary question.

Third, Khan said was that “birth spacing also belongs inside the nutritional agenda, rather than besides it”.

Punjab government’s special secretary, Aurangzaib Haider Khan, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/ Tanveer Shahzad

2:57pm - Govt official says Punjab carries majority of nutritional burden

Punjab government’s special secretary, Aurangzaib Haider Khan, delivering his address, said that Punjab shouldered the majority of the country’s nutritional burden due to the size of its population

“Let me be direct on what has moved in this scenario: Stunting among children under five has fallen from 36pc in 2018 to 27pc now.”

However, the government official held that the progress made was insufficient, as “more than one in four children“ remain stunted, leading up to around 5.5m children across the province.

2:52pm - Minister says fathers must recognise a child’s nutrition as their responsibility

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that public service messaging on nutrition must address the whole family, not just the mother.

“Too often, we place the entire burden of a child’s nutrition on women, while decisions about food purchases, healthcare and women’s workloads may be taken by other members of the family. A mother cannot carry this responsibility alone,” he said.

“Fathers must understand that nutrition is also their responsibility,” he said.

2:50pm - Minister calls for improving public service messaging

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar highlighted the need for the right kind of messaging to tackle malnutrition. He said that communication could nutrition outcomes if it was done differently.

“Public service messaging must move beyond telling people that malnutrition is a serious problem. Every message must give families practical steps they can take. Every message should have a result-oriented approach,” he said.

He said that awareness programmes often focused on the problem rather than the solution.

2:44pm - Info minister says malnutrition not simply a health issues

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that malnutrition was not simply a health issue.

“It is a moral challenge, an economic imperative and a national emergency,” he said. The minister went on to say that malnutrition was shaped by maternal health, feeding practices, unsafe water, inadequate healthcare, climate vulnerabilities and unequal access to essential services.

He further said that the Act for Nutrition conference should not be a one-off event, saying it should be an “action plan which we can implement throughout the year”.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad

2:40pm - Info minister stresses need for communication, awareness to tackle malnutrition

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, in his address, said that communication and awareness were essential for tackling malnutrition. He hailed DawnMedia group for raising awareness of the issue.

He said that more than 40pc of children in Pakistan were stunted, while maternal mortality rate was 155 deaths per 100,000 live births.

“Malnutrition costs Pakistan more than $17bn annually. If the right kind of strategy can be deployed across the country, the impact it would have on our gross domestic growth would benefit the common man,” he said.

“Behind every stunted child is potential that may never be fully realised. Behind every malnourished mother is a family at greater risk. And behind every year of inaction is another generation beginning life at a disadvantage,” he said.

2:00pm - Lunch break

1:40pm - UK expert stresses need for safely managed water and sanitation

Oliver Cumming, the environmental health lead at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, said: “The prospect of safely managed water and sanitation in Pakistan is not something which can be achieved tomorrow, and it is not as simple as shifting gears that you go from basic to safely managed.”

However, he suggested that recognition towards the goal could lead to universal access to safely managed WASH services sooner rather than later.

“We have to be realistic that it will not happen tomorrow, but putting in place the investment, the political arguments […] universal access to safely managed services can become possible within a decade,” he added.

“This is where we need to get if we really want to solve the problem of chronic malnutrition.”

1:25pm - Expert says water quality a ‘big issue’ for Pakistan

Dr Saima Khan — a water, sanitation and hygiene policy specialist — called for targeting the 36 districts in the country contributing to stunting in children. She said that WASH infrastructure investments should be done in these districts.

She also said that water quality was a “big issue” for Pakistan. She said that the country’s northern areas, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan had no infrastructure for sanitation or sewerage. She said that this was deteriorating the quality of drinking water in these areas.

1:05pm - WB official calls for understanding WASH-related drivers of malnutrition

Senior water specialist at the World Bank, Basharat Saeed, underscored the significance of gaining a “sophisticated understanding” of WASH-related drivers behind child malnutrition.

“You need to look at what are the processes at a given location that are leading to the accumulation of faecal waste, accumulation in a way that it is exposing sensitive ecosystem and exposing people to faecal pathogens,” Saeed said.

He added that it should also be made possible to track the common pathways for oral transmission for faecal material.

“If you can map that out at the start of a programme design, then you know what sort of WASH investment is needed,” he said, stressing the need for a sophisticated understanding of WASH-related drivers of malnutrition.

He added that as a result of adopting such an approach, the “proposed solution will also become slightly more comprehensive”.

Senior water specialist at the World Bank, Basharat Saeed, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Muhammad Asim

12:49pm - UK expert says water and sanitation alone cannot end stunting

Oliver Cumming, the environmental health lead at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, said that water and sanitation alone cannot end stunting, but it was essential part of the comprehensive strategies needed to address it.

He said that for the water and sanitation sector, nutrition was often peripheral, adding that this needed to change.

He said that 20pc of children in South Asia were stunted at birth, highlighting the need for prevention and an integrated approach to the issue.

12:45pm - WaterAid official calls for moving towards delivering multisectoral approach

Country director at WaterAid, Mian Muhammad Junaid, stressed that the conversation on a multisectoral approach needed to move beyond talking and towards financing and delivering results.

“We are working in silos; we still tend to organise ourselves in sectors, where nutrition sits in one policy sector, health in another, water and sanitation somewhere else, climate separately, social protection is another,” Junaid said.

He went on to note that a child did not experience these boundaries; rather, it was a lived reality for them.

“This is where I think Pakistan needs to move from talking about a multisectoral approach to actually financing and delivering one,” he added.

12:41pm - WaterAid official says child’s environment important for addressing malnutrition

In his keynote speech, Mian Muhammad Junaid, the country director for WaterAid, raised alarm at the impact of lack of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services on a child’s development and nutrition.

“A child cannot be well nourished if the environment in which the child grows is making them sick,” he said. He said WASH services were often an “important but missed” aspect of addressing malnutrition.

“WASH is a part of nutrition,“ Junaid said.

“A child may receive the right food, nutritional counselling, cash transfer and access to health facilities, but if the child is repeatedly exposed to contaminated drinking water, faecal contamination, poor sanitation and an unhealthy environment, we are asking that child to grow and develop against very difficult odds,” he said.

Mian Muhammad Junaid, the country director for WaterAid, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Muhammad Asim

12:40pm - Panel discussion on contribution of dirty water, poor sanitation to stunting begins

A panel discussion on how dirty water and poor sanitation contribute to stunting has now begun.

12:38pm - BISP official says policies, legislation remain ‘only on paper’

Tehmina Gulzar, the deputy director of nutrition at the Benazir Income Support Programme, said that hygiene, agricultural, sanitation sectors had to come together to respond to malnutrition.

She said that BISP had trained doctors, paramedical staff and teachers on adolescent nutrition to bring knowledge to communities.

She also said that while policies and legislation were drafted, they were “only on paper”.

“We need to bring them into practice. All sectors are working on [nutrition], but they are fragmented efforts,” she said, highlighting the need for the digital integration of all sectors.

12:31pm - Expert says malnutrition not ‘poverty-related’

Dr Farhana Memon, the programme director of Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health, dispelled the perception that malnutrition was tied to poverty.

“It is said that malnutrition is just poverty-related; I don’t think so. I have been in the field for 27 years, and whenever I ask a woman what she has eaten for breakfast, she will tell me she had tea and rusk,” Dr Memon said.

“We have failed to convince her that she can get an egg for the same cost,” she said.

“Let’s take an example of two issues in public health — breastfeeding and micronutrient deficiencies — these are not poverty-related; it’s knowledge-related,” she said.

12:15pm - BISP official says social protection programmes can play ‘significant role’ in improving nutrition outcomes

Tehmina Gulzar, the deputy director of nutrition at the Benazir Income Support Programme, said that social protection programmes can play a “significant role” in improving nutrition outcomes.

She added that BISP was a very good example of how social protection programmes could contribute toward human capital development.

She also said that BISP had a huge collection of data that could be used by different sectors involved in addressing nutrition.

Tehmina Gulzar, the deputy director of nutrition at the Benazir Income Support Programme, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Muhammad Asim

12:01pm - Expert says nutrition cannot be viewed in isolation

CEO of the Pakistan Alliance on Early Childhood Development Khadija Khan warned against viewing nutrition in isolation.

“Because for holistic development, you need a complete package and that package is described in the nurturing care framework, which is talking about good health, adequate nutrition, responsive caregiving, safety, security and early learning opportunity.”

She held that until and unless these inputs were met, it was not possible to achieve holistic child development.

“We do talk about a multisectoral approach and an integrated approach, but still the families are knocking on different doors for different services. In reality, we do not really give integrated services to our children,” Khan added.

11:49am - Non-profit head says people do not ‘believe in the system’

Shahid Lone, the chairman of the Allah Walay Foundation, said that if policymakers and those responsible for implementation did not put their “soul” into what they were doing, then what they were aiming for “would never work”.

He acknowledged that his take was more “philosophical”. He highlighted that government officials say one thing on stage and another when they are behind the scenes.

“We have policies, we have departments, but we have people who do not believe in the system,” he said. He questioned how those who did not have vision or believed in their work could implement policies.

Shahid Lone, the chairman of the Allah Walay Foundation, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Muhammad Asim

11:37am - ‘Behaviour of healthcare providers pathetic’

Dr Farhana Memon, the programme director of Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health, also criticised the behaviour of healthcare workers.

“The behaviour of healthcare providers is pathetic,” Dr Memon said, noting that most healthcare workers did not counsel patients on family planning, nutrition, or vaccination.

“We have been trying to change the behaviour of the community for the past decade, but now it is time to change the behaviour of healthcare providers.”

“If a person or a woman comes into contact with you, please don’t waste the opportunity,” she urged.

11:34am - Expert decries lack of dedicated funding for nutrition

Programme director of Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health Dr Farhana Memon decried the lack of funds to address malnutrition.

“If you want to [translate] policies into action, you should have some cost,” she said, adding that donors largely funded efforts to end malnutrition.

“This is not the solution,” Memon remarked, adding that nutrition should be treated as a separate entity.

She further urged that the government must utilise every access point as an opportunity to counsel families about nutrition.

Programme director of Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health Dr Farhana Memon speaks at the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Muhammad Asim

11:25am - Session on multisectoral approach to nutrition begins

A session on the multisectoral approach to nutrition has now begun.

11:20am - KP CM says govt working on addressing malnutrition

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, in a video message, said that facilitation centres were being established to address malnutrition among pregnant women and young children.

He said that the provincial government, under PTI founder Imran Khan’s vision, was working on this issue and others.

He ended by thanking DawnMedia for highlighting malnutrition and other social issues.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi’s video message at the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad

11:10am - Govt official calls for cohesive national narrative on malnutrition

Dr Shabana Haider, member (population) in the Planning Commission of Pakistan, stressed the need for a cohesive national narrative in addressing malnutrition.

“Do not go switching your national narrative; sometimes it is said that two kids are enough, sometimes it is one, and sometimes you ask women to time their pregnancies. Please develop a narrative that you can lead on and that everybody — from development partners to private sector — can converge on,” she said.

11:00am - Govt official says nutritional challenges cannot be addressed without acknowledging population dynamics

Dr Shabana Haider, member (population) in the Planning Commission of Pakistan, said that nutritional challenges could not be addressed without acknowledging population dynamics and demographic dividends could not be reaped without investing in nutrition.

She said that while Pakistan had done a lot on the policy side, the documents themselves were not enough.

“We are very good at framing policies … sorry, excuse me, this has to change … let’s all recognise that our priority has not been population,” she said, adding that population had been neglected as a subject.

10:50am - KP govt official says malnutrition, family planning interlinked

Dr Fazal Majeed, the director of nutrition at the Directorate General Health Services for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, said that Pakistan had a stunting growth rate of 40pc, adding that it was 48pc in KP’s merged districts.

He also said that almost 40pc of women of reproductive age were also anaemic, calling the figures “alarming”.

“Malnutrition, family planning … are interlinked,” he said. He said some of the barriers in KP were fragmented delivery points, geographical and security-related.

Dr Fazal Majeed, the director of nutrition at the Directorate General Health Services for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference, — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad

10:35am - Public health professional says history of Pakistan’s health programmes ‘one of isolation’

Dr Talib Lashari, a public health professional with the Sindh government’s health department, said that the nexus between nutrition and family planning was “well established but poorly practised in Pakistan”.

“The history of Pakistan’s public health programmes and initiatives is one of isolation. All the programmes have been well-designed and, to some extent, properly funded, but they were implemented in isolation,” he said.

10:24am - Govt adviser says nutrition needs to be reclassified as a capital expenditure

Adnan Pasha Siddiqui, the adviser to the minister of finance, said that nutrition needed to be reclassified as a capital expenditure rather than as an expense.

“So this single accounting decision suppresses the investment narrative permanently … these are fundamental flaws we need to correct,” he said.

Adnan Pasha Siddiqui, the adviser to the minister of finance, addresses the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad

10:17am - Govt adviser says lack of investment in nutrition hurts Pakistan’s GDP

Adnan Pasha Siddiqui, the adviser to the minister of finance, said that burgeoning population and lack of resources were a “collective failure of capital investment”.

“We are reflecting everything nutrition-related as a health expenditure … every rupee that is withheld from a pregnant women’s diet is a deduction from the country’s gross domestic product in the future,” he said. He said that in the country, nutrition was divided across several sectors.

Siddiqui said that the annual loss from malnutrition was $17bn. He said that in South Asia, labour productivity was suppressed because of nutrition.

“And it is a structural liability to our sovereign credit profile,” he said.

10:08am - World Bank official says nutrition is viewed through ‘a human capital lens’

Sara Shahzad, the senior health specialist from the World Bank, said that the group had 10-year country partnership framework with the government of Pakistan focused on six priority areas, one of which was stunting reduction.

“So the way the World Bank looks at population stabilisation and nutrition, specifically the stunting agenda, is through a human capital lens,” she said.

Talking about stunting, she said that 30-40pc of it occurred before a child was born.

“So, the first 1,000 days are absolutely critical but also the adolescence period,” she said.

Sara Shahzad, the senior health specialist from the World Bank, speaks at the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad

9:58am - Expert highlights ‘experimentation’ in Pakistan’s population planning

Dr Ali Mir, the country director for the Population Council, said that there was always a tendency in Pakistan of “making the same mistakes again and again”. Talking about Pakistan’s previous population reforms, he highlighted wavering political commitment and policy inconsistency.

“We never explicitly had a population policy till 2002. It was always couched in development planning,” he said.

He said that due to this, Pakistan was constantly “experimenting”. Dr Mir said that now things were moving in the right direction, with the establishment of the Population Council.

Dr Ali Mir, the country director for the Population Council, speaks at the Act for Nutrition conference. — White Star/Tanveer Shahzad

9:55am - Doctor says nutrition is ‘not an isolated event’

Dr Saima Hamid, the programme and research lead at the Population Council, said that Pakistan’s population growth rate is at 2.55pc. She said that in 28 years, the country’s population would double, putting a huge burden on resources.

“This clearly is a challenge of not just the quantity but also the quality of diet. We need to ensure that diverse nutrition reaches those most vulnerable,” she said.

She also said that Pakistan’s domestic food security was on the decline, adding that “nutrition is not just an isolated event”.

“One sector isn’t really responsible … there is a clear intersection of nutrition, food security, health, purchasing power,” she said.

9:52am - Session on population and resources has begun

A session on how a nation cannot feed, educate or employ what it cannot count on sustaining has now begun.

9:50am - 2nd day of conference begins

The second day of the conference begins with a short film titled Leaky Guts from the Aga Khan University.

World.title: Security forces kill 15 terrorists trying to cross into Pakistan through Afghan border: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces have killed 15 terrorists who were trying to infiltrate into Pakistan through its border with Afghanistan, the military’s media affairs wing said on Thursday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the terrorists had tried to cross into Pakistan’s North Waziristan district on the night between August 31 and September 1.

Their movement, however, was detected by security forces, the statement said, adding that the troops “responded professionally and with patience to engage them”.

“As a result of precise and skillful engagement that lasted for 36 hours, 15 khawarij belonging to India-sponsored Fitna-al-Khawarij” were killed, the statement added.

The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

ISPR said that during the sanitisation operation after the engagement, large quantities of weapons and ammunition were recovered from the slain terrorists. This further “exposed the nefarious designs of khawarij and their facilitators seeking to disrupt peace and stability in the country,” the military’s media wing said.

It said the incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border once again vindicated Pakistan’s “persistent stance regarding the abject failure of the Afghan Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil to the terrorist organisation under their patronage for cross-border terrorism”.

“The Afghan Taliban regime has consistently failed to ensure effective border management and honor its international obligations,” ISPR said.

It further stated that a “sanitisation operation is being conducted to eliminate any other India-sponsored khariji found in the area as [the] relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” ISPR stated.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for foiling an infiltration attempt near the Pak-Afghan border in North Waziristan, state-run PTV reported.

“The security forces, demonstrating utmost professional skill, patience and courage, have reduced the impure intentions of the terrorists to dust,” he said in a statement.

He said the Azm-i-Istehkam campaign against terrorism would continue with full force and determination until the menace of terrorism was uprooted from the country, according to the statement.

President Asif Ali Zardari also paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operation, according to a statement issued by the Presidency.

“The resolve of the security forces to defend the borders of the beloved homeland and protect peace and stability is commendable,” the president was quoted as saying.

“No permission will be granted to terrorist elements operating under foreign patronage to spread unrest in Pakistan,” he added.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for foiling the infiltration attempt, saying they had reduced the enemy’s “nefarious intentions to dust”, according to a statement issued by his ministry.

The latest action comes as Islamabad continues to stress that the Afghan Taliban put an end to the use of Afghan soil by terrorists, particularly for attacks in Pakistan.

Despite recent diplomatic developments suggesting a renewed push to ease tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, the Foreign Office on Wednesday remained firm that meaningful progress in relations would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against TTP and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

The FO spokesperson’s remarks, during a weekly briefing, came amid renewed diplomatic activity, including Chinese Special Envoy Yue Xiaoyong’s visit to Islamabad to revive the Urumqi process aimed at preventing further escalation, and an invitation to Afghan ambassador Sardar Shakeb to speak at the National Defence University.

Islamabad, however, sees little proof that the Taliban have moved beyond containing TTP activities.

The latest UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team report noted that the Taliban had relocated around 2,000 TTP fighters and their families away from areas bordering Pakistan, and that Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada had warned the group against attacks on Pakistan — but also that Taliban support for the TTP continued as the group escalated attacks and expanded its organisational structure.

For Islamabad, relocating terrorists does not amount to dismantling the command, training and logistical networks that remain at the centre of its concerns.

World.title: LHC's Justice Raheel Kamran resigns as judge
World.content:
LAHORE: Lahore High Court’s (LHC) Justice Raheel Kamran Sheikh resigned as a judge on Thursday, saying he wanted to pursue legal scholarship, policy research and comparative judicial practice.

He sent his resignation letter, dated Sept 3, to President Asif Ali Zardari under Article 206 of the Constitution.

In the letter, seen by Dawn, Justice Sheikh said his years on the bench had been the most formative and fulfilling period of his professional life.

He wrote that after “deep and sustained reflection”, he had concluded that his further growth as a jurist — and his ability to contribute to the rule of law and access to justice — would be better served by turning to legal scholarship, policy research and comparative judicial practice.

Justice Sheikh thanked his senior colleagues on the bench for their guidance and his staff for their support, saying he was leaving with an “enduring commitment to the Constitution and the rule of law”.

A copy of the resignation was also sent to the LHC registrar.

Justice Sheikh, a graduate of the London School of Economics and a barrister of the Middle Temple, has been serving as an LHC judge since May 2021.

Before his elevation to the bench, he was an elected member of the Pakistan Bar Council for a period of five years (2016-2020) and also chaired its Human Rights Committee. His legal practice covered public law, commercial law, taxation and human rights.

He is the son of senior lawyer Akram Sheikh, a former president of the Supreme Court Bar Association.

He was due to reach his superannuation on Jan 30, 2036.

World.title: ‘Unreasonable’ to say cricket in Pakistan has finished: PCB chief Naqvi
World.content:
Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi has labelled claims of cricket being finished in the country as “unreasonable”, citing Pakistan’s improved rankings under his tenure to prove otherwise.

“South Africa lost to Namibia, India lost to Ireland. At least check there, has cricket finished there?” said Naqvi while speaking to reporters in London on Wednesday.

The PCB has received much criticism for the mid-series shakeup during the national team’s Test tour of England, in which seven players and two coaches from the initial squad were replaced after heavy defeats in Headingley and Lords.

The decision gathered the ire of fans, pundits and former players alike. Former Pakistan captain Azhar Ali was one of them — while speaking to Dawn on Wednesday, he said that difficult decisions like these cause “insecurity among the players,” and that they need to be made within stable frameworks.

Naqvi, however, believes it inappropriate to claim that Pakistan cricket is at its worst, and that the white-ball teams have shown improvement in the recent past.

“You used to be ranked eighth in ODIs, which has now gone up to fifth. You have had six ODI series, out of which you have won four, but still, our cricket is finished,” he said, resorting to sarcasm.

“Our success rate has gone up from 24 pc to 73pc, and I’m not talking about just one or the other specific match, but still, our cricket is finished.”

Naqvi added that while everyone retained the right of criticism and to ask why certain games had been lost, and that the team’s performance in Test cricket required much improvement, it was unfair to deem it a terminal decline.

“Those players who have never achieved anything in their lives, when they talk along these lines, that’s unreasonable,” he said, adding that he sought opinions from ex-players constantly.

He also said it is called a problem regardless of whether players are retained or removed, and that ultimately the board is “only answerable for the results.”

“Sometimes there are mistakes made in selection as well. I am answerable for that, and we need to work on it,” he said, adding that sometimes it was necessary to remove players if they do not perform.

“The purpose is not to kick someone out, but to change them in case they are not clicking,” he said, giving the example of Salman Ali Agha, who was stand-in captain for the first Test but was subsequently dropped from the playing XI and then the squad altogether.

He added that it was not possible to take a team from number nine to number one in a matter of three or six months, and that there was “a long way to go”.

“These are facts you can check and verify yourselves, if they are wrong, we are responsible,” he said, “but the way you are demotivating the boys, please stop doing that.”

Naqvi also added that the scorn for these decisions has come as criticism of himself.

“Actually, they just want to drive me out, nothing else.”

“If someone has resentment towards me, by all means criticise me personally. But don’t target cricket.”

The Pakistan cricket team, along with Naqvi were welcomed to the Buckingham Palace on Wednesday, for an audience with King Charles. The team will play the third and final Test against England at Edgbaston in Birmingham on September 9.

World.title: 'World in danger zone': UN says El Nino likely to intensify, may become strongest ever recorded
World.content:
El Nino could be the strongest since records began four decades ago, the United Nations’ climate agency warned on Thursday, with the UN chief warning the world is in the “danger zone of extreme weather”.

The naturally-occurring weather phenomenon is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead and is near certain to persist through to February, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said.

El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.

“If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began — so literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva.

El Nino will peak towards the end of this year — though its knock-on impacts for the climate will continue well into 2027, said the WMO.

Heat in the oceans releases more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the following year.

The powerful 2023-24 El Nino contributed to 2024 being the warmest year on record, and “we should not be surprised if this record is broken”, Saulo added.

“El Nino is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat,” the WMO said.

El Nino is a natural climate phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.

But scientists expect it will exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming from burning fossil fuels, while amping-up weather extremes.

“El Nino is being supersized before our eyes,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres.

“The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather.

“The race now is between rising risks and our commitment to take climate action and protect people. We must win that race.”

‘Massive blow’ to economies

“This exceptional El Nino … has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world”, said Saulo.

“We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Nino intensifies.”

She put disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water on notice, saying there was “no time to lose” in getting ready.

El Nino typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.

Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.

“Fuelled by exceptionally warm ocean conditions across the tropical Pacific, El Nino is expected to strengthen further during the coming months to a very strong intensity,” the WMO said.

The UN agency classifies El Nino events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong — meaning it is set to reach the highest level out of four.

The WMO said there was an “exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100 per cent” that El Nino will continue through to February.

Pacific Ocean heating up

El Nino can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometres away from the tropical Pacific.

Every El Nino is different, but major events often follow familiar patterns. This includes drought across parts of the Amazon, Indonesia and Australia, disrupted monsoons in India, and shifting rainfall throughout the tropics.

For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures “across almost all land areas”, alongside rainfall patterns showing a “pronounced and classic atmospheric response to the strong Pacific El Nino”, the UN’s weather and climate agency said.

The index that measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average 1.5 degrees Celcius above normal between May and July.

Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from around 2.2 degrees Celsius to 2.6 degrees Celsius above average, indicating continued El Nino intensification.

In some areas, subsurface ocean temperatures were more than 8 degrees Celsius above average during July and early August.

World.title: Pakistan raises $3bn through dual-tranche Eurobond sale
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has raised a record $3 billion — its single largest international capital market transaction — through a dual-tranche Eurobond sale that drew nearly $6bn in orders, the Ministry of Finance said on Thursday.

In a statement, it said: “The transaction attracted nearly $6bn in orders — almost twice the amount issued — from a broad and diversified base of institutional investors across global markets and continents.”

“The successful transaction marks a major milestone in Pakistan’s renewed and increasingly diversified access to international capital markets, demonstrating strong investor confidence and Pakistan’s ability to access global funding markets at significant scale,” the ministry added.

The transaction includes $1.75bn through a 5.5-year bond at a coupon rate of 7.5 per cent and $1.25bn through a 10-year bond at 7.9pc, the ministry said.

Pakistan’s last most expensive Eurobond was raised more than a decade ago at an 8.25pc interest rate during the tenure of the PML-N government. It reached maturity a couple of years ago and has already been repaid.

The finance ministry said on Thursday that the total global demand for Pakistani paper amounted to $6bn.

“The competitive pricing across both maturities, together with strong demand extending to the 10-year tenor, demonstrates Pakistan’s ability to mobilise sizeable longer-term financing as international investors reassess the country’s improving macroeconomic and credit fundamentals,” it said. However, the significance of this transaction goes well beyond the amount raised, it added.

“The transaction also represents an important milestone in Pakistan’s broader road to market strategy,” the ministry said.

It said that after the successful inaugural Panda Bond and improvements in Pakistan’s sovereign credit profile, this was the first issuance under the country’s renewed strategic Global Medium-Term Note (GMTN) Programme — creating a platform for diversified access to international capital markets.

“The objective is not simply to raise additional debt. Pakistan is pursuing a broader strategy of active sovereign liability management — diversifying financing sources, extending maturities, reducing refinancing and rollover risks, and creating opportunities to replace shorter-term and more expensive obligations with longer-duration, competitively priced financing, where economically beneficial,” the ministry said.

“Pakistan has already pursued substantial early retirement of domestic debt ahead of maturity. Extending that discipline to external financing is part of the same objective: Borrow better. Extend maturities. Diversify funding. Reduce refinancing risk. Improve the sovereign debt profile. This is the difference between simply borrowing and actively managing the sovereign balance sheet,” it added.

It said that over the past three years, Pakistan’s improving economic trajectory had increasingly been recognised through successive sovereign credit-rating upgrades and renewed access to international capital markets.

“Now, global investors have reinforced that assessment with billions of dollars of actual capital,” it said.

“The depth of the order book, its geographically diversified institutional investor base, and substantial demand for a 10-year Pakistan sovereign instrument together provide a powerful market-based signal of renewed confidence in Pakistan’s medium and long-term trajectory,” the ministry said.

“Three years of rebuilding credibility; nearly $6bn of global investor demand, and a record $3bn issued in a single transaction — it is a landmark moment in Pakistan’s journey from economic stabilisation towards sustainable growth — and a stronger platform for the road ahead,” it concluded.

In April, the government initially raised $500 million through a three-year Eurobond under its GMTN Programme at a coupon of 6.975pc. The issue was subsequently increased to $750m through a $250m green-shoe option after stronger-than-expected investor demand. The bond matures in April 2029.

Pakistan has also repaid a $1.4 billion Eurobond that matured in April, allowing the government to re-establish a pricing benchmark in international debt markets after several years of relying heavily on multilateral, bilateral and commercial financing.

The latest offering extends the maturity profile beyond the three-year tenor used in April, with the proposed five and 10-year tranches providing a test of investors’ willingness to hold Pakistani sovereign debt for longer periods.

World.title: NCCIA issues fresh notices to Momina Iqbal, PML-N MPA Chadhar after new evidence emerges in harassment case
World.content:
LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Thursday issued fresh notices to television actor Momina Iqbal and PML-N MPA Saqib Chadhar after new evidence emerged against them in the case pertaining to Iqbal’s alleged harassment.

Iqbal publicly accused Chadhar of online harassment, cyberbullying and threats earlier this year. Her allegations, initially made through social media, triggered widespread attention, and the NCCIA registered a case against Chadhar under several provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) and the Pakistan Penal Code.

Both parties have been summoned for Friday (Sept 4) at the NCCIA office in Lahore. The agency has also constituted a special investigation team to conduct a fresh inquiry into the matter.

NCCIA Punjab’s Deputy Director Waqas Saeed told Dawn that a special team headed by a deputy director would examine the newly obtained digital evidence, along with previously available records in this case.

“The team has been given one month to complete its investigation and submit a report to the NCCIA director general,” he said, adding that further legal action would be decided in light of the findings of the investigation.

The spokesperson said that it would be premature to declare either of the individuals “guilty” or “innocent” before the completion of the inquiry.

Court disposes of pleas

A Lahore court also disposed of PML-N MPA Saqib Chadhar’s and his wife’s pre-arrest interim bail petitions as withdrawn, after the investigating officer said the arrest of the suspects was not required at the present stage.

At the last hearing on July 28, then-investigating officer (IO), SHO Najam Bajwa from the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), had informed the sessions court that Chadhar had been found guilty after investigation.

However, the new IO, Hassan Sajjad Naqvi, told the court today that the investigation had changed and the suspects’ arrest was not required at this stage.

The IO had separately summoned Iqbal on September 1, according to the summons order seen by Dawn.

The order said that the suspects had requested a re-investigation of the case on the “basis of some new defence evidence […] Accordingly, your statement regarding the fresh evidence has to recorded”.

Iqbal was also present at the hearing, where the IO informed the court of the development. Following this, Chadhar and his wife withdrew their bail petitions, and the court subsequently disposed of the pleas as withdrawn.

The case

In a social media post in May, Iqbal had alleged that she had been subjected to “online harassment, cyberbullying and death threats for a long time”.

She claimed that both she and her family had suffered severe mental stress and trauma because of the alleged conduct of an MPA, without naming the accused.

“A member of the provincial assembly belonging to the PML-N has been threatening me for an extended period. I repeatedly reported the matter to the NCCIA and the Federal Investigation Agency, but no action was taken,” she stated.

Subsequently, the PML-N’s “top leadership directed the NCCIA to immediately entertain the actor’s complaint and initiate action against the ruling party MPA if the allegations are proven”, a source had told Dawn. The source added that the Punjab Chief Minister’s Office also wanted to clear its name following Iqbal’s allegations against it.

Following these developments, the NCCIA summoned Iqbal and Chadhar on May 21. The agency’s Punjab head Muhammad Ali Waseem said the two were summoned after the NCCIA received Iqbal’s complaint.

The actor had lodged a formal complaint after being summoned for questioning in May, alleging that Chadhar, his wife and other associates had subjected her to a sustained campaign of cyber harassment, stalking, criminal intimidation, blackmail and threats.

Chadhar’s counsel maintained that the two had known each other for several years and disputed the actor’s allegations.

A day after they recorded their statements , Iqbal filed an application with Lahore’s Chung Police for the registration of a first information report against Chadhar.

In her application, she alleged that the PML-N MPA had been making threatening calls to harass her and her fiance. She claimed that the lawmaker turned abusive when she refused his marriage proposal, after it transpired that he was already married to two women.

Subsequently, Chadhar began blackmailing her, she alleged, also mentioning WhatsApp messages and video calls from the suspect in her application. She further alleged that the MPA also sent the same threatening messages to her sister’s mobile phone.

Meanwhile, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also warned in a post on X that any attempt to exert political pressure, abuse influence, or exploit a woman by threatening to release “personal content” in the case involving Iqbal and Chadhar would be met with “firm and uncompromising action.”

World.title: Unicef estimates 20 million children suffered online sexual abuse in one year
World.content:
About 20 million internet-using children across 21 countries were subjected to sexual exploitation or abuse on digital platforms in a single year, with most cases occurring on social media platforms, a new report by the UN children’s charity said on Thursday.

More than one in five children aged 12 to 17 across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe experienced at least one form of sexual abuse or exploitation on online platforms in the year before being surveyed, the Unicef report estimated.

Roughly 15m children in the countries surveyed were exposed to unwanted sexual content, 9m were pressured into sexual conversations or sharing sexual images, and 4m had sexual images shared without their consent, the report found.

The number of children subjected to this abuse globally is certain to run into many tens of millions, it said.

The research, which Unicef described as one of the largest studies of its kind, was based on national representative surveys collected between 2020 and 2025 of around 21,000 internet-using children in the 21 countries, which included Pakistan, Kenya, Brazil and Serbia.

Social media focus

Almost 60 per cent of reported abuse occurred on social media platforms, led by Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok, while 14pc took place in online gaming, the report found.

A spokesperson for Meta, which owns Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, said the surveys go as far back as 2020, before the company introduced protections Unicef recommends such as automatically defaulting teens into private accounts and preventing adults from messaging teens they are not connected to. It added that it defines WhatsApp as a private messaging app and not a social media platform.

“While the report doesn’t provide any specific evidence of abuse, we’ll continue to fight child exploitation aggressively across our apps and support law enforcement in prosecuting the criminals behind it,” the Meta spokesperson said.

Snapchat pointed Reuters to a blog post by Global Head of Platform Safety Jacqueline Beauchere, who said the company was actively combating online sexual extortion through proactive detection, account removals, user reporting tools and safety features designed to protect vulnerable users.

TikTok said it has built a range of safeguards to protect minors, including restricting certain features for younger users, making accounts for under-18s private by default, and using technology to detect potentially predatory behaviour.

The Unicef report said more than half the cases involved someone the child already knew, including friends, relatives or romantic partners, while 38pc of children first encountered the perpetrator online.

Fewer than 1pc of cases involving children were reported to the police, a social worker or a helpline, according to the research.

The report also highlighted growing concerns over artificial intelligence. Across nine countries where data was collected, an estimated 1.1m children reported having AI-generated sexual images or videos created depicting them.

Children who experienced tech-facilitated sexual exploitation were around four times more likely to report suicidal thoughts or self-harm and reported significantly higher levels of anxiety than their peers, the research said.

“These experiences cause profound emotional and mental distress. Many children suffer in silence, unsure where to turn for help,” Unicef Executive Director Catherine Russell said in a statement.

Unicef urged governments and technology companies to strengthen safety measures on digital platforms, update laws to address evolving forms of abuse including AI-generated content, and improve child protection and reporting systems.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.
